  data plane (`GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_ID=${CLUSTER_ID_B}`), with the same rejection semantics as a real second cluster:
  registration deactivated → `403 regional cluster authentication failed`, header/token mismatch → 403,
  B's own credentials → 200 and it claims this round's candidate.
- Cleanup obligations (regardless of whether the body passed or failed): delete the Pod first, then publish a durable revision without B (removing only B,
  never overwriting others' new registrations wholesale), then delete the Secret, ConfigMap
  and namespace under uid/resourceVersion preconditions. The evidence `synthetic_secondary` records the generation before/during/after publishing, the Pod
  identity, the result of each cleanup step, and the proof that "the registry has no B, the namespace and Pod do not exist, A's registration is byte-for-byte
  unchanged"; the case evidence carries `secondary_registered: true` and
  `secondary_kind: "synthetic-logical"`. Incomplete cleanup or any residue is FAIL. Both the registration and the Pod carry a
  30-minute lifetime (`synthetic_expires_at` / `activeDeadlineSeconds`), so B also expires on its own if the runner dies midway;
  residue is removed by hand using the uids recorded in `cases/<case>/synthetic-secondary.json`.
- This fully covers credential isolation, state isolation, and isolation of identical node/job/attempt IDs,
  but it **cannot** cover "one physical cluster going offline as a whole". The latter must wait until a second physical cluster is attached and
  `GF-REGIONAL-ISO-006` is executed; until then that gate is recorded as unverified and must not be claimed as passed.

---

## 4. BOOT: Regional-mode fail-closed startup guards

This group verifies that the control plane **refuses to start** when its configuration is
unsafe, rather than running with a dangerous configuration.
All cases run on a **separate, disposable validation Deployment**
(`gpu-fault-api-guard-probe`) and never modify the serving `gpu-fault-api-ha`.

### 4.0 Preparing the disposable probe (shared fixture for BOOT-001~009)

Early versions had only one sentence here, "manually set replicas to 1 and remove the
labels related to the Service selector", which was on-the-spot reasoning, neither
reproducible nor safe. Below is the complete, **directly executable** recipe.

Before the runner fetches the probe Pod it must wait for the current Deployment's rollout to
complete, then confirm there is exactly one Pod and that it is not terminating.
A rollout, API read or manifest-parse failure blocks immediately; even when `probe_pod_name`
sits inside a command substitution, it must propagate failure explicitly and must not
keep using the old Pod or treat empty output as success.

**Why a simple `sed` rename is not enough** (four real risks, each of which must be closed by
the steps below):

1. **The Service would route production traffic to the probe.**
   The selectors of `gpu-fault-api` (ClusterIP) and `gpu-fault-api-nlb` (LoadBalancer)
   are both `app: gpu-fault-api-ha`. If only `metadata.name` is changed and the Pod
   label is not, the probe Pod becomes an endpoint of both Services as soon as it is Ready,
   which amounts to wiring a deliberately misconfigured instance into production.
   **The Pod template label must be changed as well**, and once the label changes,
   `selector.matchLabels` must change too (a Deployment's selector is immutable, but this
   is a newly created object, so there is no immutability problem).
2. **Anti-affinity + topologySpread would collide.**
   Production uses `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`
   anti-affinity + `whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule`, both with topologyKey
   `kubernetes.io/hostname`, and the cluster has only 3 CPU nodes, all 3 already taken by
   production. After the label change these two constraints no longer match the production
   Pods, so the probe can be scheduled;
   but **this is exactly the second reason the label must change** -- if
   `app: gpu-fault-api-ha` were kept, the probe would sit in `Pending/Unschedulable` and
   never enter `CrashLoopBackOff`, and the case would be misjudged as PASS because
   "the Pod is not Ready" (false green).
3. **A probe that gets past the settings guards writes the registry into Aurora.**
   The registry/mutual-exclusion validation of `BOOT-001/002/003` is now done in
   `Settings.from_mapping()`, before the store is constructed, so it does not write to the
   database. But the assembly guards of BOOT-004/005/006/009 and the positive branches of
   BOOT-007/008 enter `ApplicationContext._base_context()`, where
   `save_regional_cluster()` persists the registry first. If the probe is connected to the
   production DSN, the production registry is still polluted with test data.
   **The probe must be attached to a separate database.**
4. **A PDB with the same name as production would be rejected or would wrongly protect the probe.**
   The probe creates no PDB and no Service.

**Differences between probe and production (all other fields reuse the verified production configuration)**:

| Item | Production | Probe | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `metadata.name` | `gpu-fault-api-ha` | `gpu-fault-api-guard-probe` | Does not overwrite the production object |
| Pod label `app` | `gpu-fault-api-ha` | `gpu-fault-api-guard-probe` | Escapes the Service selector and anti-affinity (risks 1, 2) |
| `replicas` | 3 | 1 | Negative cases only need one crashing Pod for a verdict |
| `GPU_FAULT_STORE_URL` | `postgres-url` of `gpu-fault-aurora` | Temporary Secret pointing at the separate database `gpu_fault_guardprobe` | Risk 3 |
| `GPU_FAULT_STORE_URL_FILE` and the DSN volume | Projected file of the production Secret | Read-only projection of the separate probe Secret; production DSN volume reference removed | The file DSN takes precedence over the parameter and the start-time environment; no production reference may remain |
| `GPU_FAULT_EXECUTOR_MODE` | `active` | `active` (unchanged) | Must stay active, otherwise the guard code never runs at all (see below) |
| Pod resources requests | ingress currently `4 CPU / 4Gi` | `250m / 1Gi`, limits unchanged | Production control-plane requests already occupy 87%–91% of the three nodes; startup-guard semantics do not depend on resource reservation |
| Notification delivery | Production SES enabled | `ALLOW_EMAIL=false`, dispatcher=false, `ACKNOWLEDGE_NO_ALERT_CHANNEL=true` | The BOOT-007/008 positive probes become Ready; fake-cluster background tasks must not mail production recipients |
| Service / NLB / PDB | Present | **Not created** | Risks 1, 4 |
| Pod Identity | `gpu-fault-control-plane` SA | Reuses the same SA | The probe only reads Secrets, no new permissions |

> `GPU_FAULT_EXECUTOR_MODE` must not be changed to `standby`: `src/gpu_fault/app/`
> **returns immediately** when `config.enabled` is false, and none of the regional guards that
> follow (from line 334 on) run. If the probe were downgraded to standby, every negative case
> would "start successfully", while their verdict is "Pod not Ready" -- another false green. This is the easiest trap to fall into in this group.

**Step P1: Environment and precondition assertions**

```bash
export AWS_REGION=us-west-2
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-west-2
export CPU_KUBECONFIG=/tmp/gpu-fault-control-plane.kubeconfig
export NAMESPACE=gpu-fault-system
export PROBE=gpu-fault-api-guard-probe
kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
  get deployment gpu-fault-api-ha \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}{" "}{.metadata.generation}{" "}{.spec.replicas}{" "}{.status.readyReplicas}{"\n"}'
```

Record the actual generation and the desired/Ready replica counts of this run; after the
whole group has run, re-check the same Deployment UID against these baselines. Do not use
fixed numbers from historical run records.

**Step P2: Create a separate database for the probe**

Run only inside an approved acceptance window. The DSN never enters local argv or ordinary
evidence. Use the same `boot_guard_isolation.py` as the runner: first read the currently
projected credentials, then clear the inherited `GPU_FAULT_STORE_URL_FILE` and `PG*`
overrides, confirm the actual database identity, and only then initialise the schema in
the separate database. Do not construct a Store directly inside a production Pod with a
renamed URL.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
CPU_API_POD="$(kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
  get pod -l app=gpu-fault-api-ha \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')"
BOOT_DB_HELPER="${REPO:?}/scripts/e2e/regional/boot_guard_isolation.py"
test -n "${CPU_API_POD}" && test -f "${BOOT_DB_HELPER}"
kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
  exec -i "${CPU_API_POD}" -- /opt/gpu-fault/control-plane/bin/python - initialize \
  < "${BOOT_DB_HELPER}"
```

**Step P3: Write the probe DSN into a temporary Secret (the password never passes through the local shell)**

The same helper builds the separate-database Secret from the currently projected
credentials. The Secret document is handed to Kubernetes only through a private pipe; do
not run the `secret` sub-operation separately in the terminal, and do not use `tee`, shell
tracing or ordinary logs to record the pipe contents. `pipefail` must be enabled so that a
failure at either end stops the run.

```bash
set -o pipefail
kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
  exec -i "${CPU_API_POD}" -- /opt/gpu-fault/control-plane/bin/python - secret \
  < "${BOOT_DB_HELPER}" \
  | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
```

The helper's initialise/cleanup output contains status only; on failure it prints only the
exception type. The Secret's base64 encoding is not redaction and must not be written into
the acceptance report. The later `derive.sh` uses the same helper to isolate both the
environment variables and the mount paths.

**Steps P4~P6: Fixture scripts (kept in the repository, never written ad hoc into `/tmp`)**

The fixture lives in **`scripts/e2e/regional/boot_guard/`** and consists of 6 files:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `derive.sh` | P4: derives the probe baseline manifest from the production Deployment into `/tmp/guard-probe-base.json` and performs 6 assertions |
| `mutate.py` | P5: single-variable mutator (`del` / `set` / `sref`) |
| `registry.py` | Registry JSON generator used by BOOT-007/008 |
| `reset.sh` | Resets the probe before every case, **polling until the Pod count reaches zero** |
| `assert.sh` | P6: asserts "not Ready + log contains the given text" |
| `cleanup.sh` | Cleanup after the whole group; **reads nothing from `/tmp`** and can run on its own |

The verdict and cleanup scripts must be versioned with the repository; `/tmp` may only hold
manifests and kubeconfigs that the repository scripts can re-derive, and the cleanup flow
must not depend on the temporary directory still existing.

Usage:

```bash
cd scripts/e2e/regional/boot_guard
./derive.sh                  # P4, run once; if /tmp was wiped, rerun this line to recover
./reset.sh                   # before every case
python3 mutate.py del GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON \
  | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
./assert.sh 'regional mode requires GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON'
```

Orchestration entry point for the whole group:

```bash
CPU_KUBECONFIG="${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" \
NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE}" \
CPU_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER="${CPU_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER}" \
AWS_REGION="${AWS_REGION}" \
RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR}" \
PYTHON=.venv/bin/python \
  scripts/e2e/regional/run_regional_boot_guard_cases.sh \
  --run-dir "${RUN_DIR}" --plan
```

After checking the targets and preflight in the plan, execute with the same environment and RUN_DIR:

```bash
PYTHON=.venv/bin/python \
  bash scripts/e2e/regional/run_regional_boot_guard_cases.sh \
  --run-dir "${RUN_DIR}" --execute --confirm BOOT_GUARD_EXECUTE \
  --maintenance-window-end "${MAINTENANCE_WINDOW_END}"
```

If the runner stops at BOOT-007/008 or later because of a fixture problem, after the fix it
may resume in the **same** `RUN_DIR` with `BOOT_GUARD_START_CASE=7` or `8`. The entry point
accepts only `1`, `7`, `8`; when resuming it first checks, case by case, that the **last
line** of each evidence file before the target case is `VERDICT PASS` (each case file ends
with exactly one line `VERDICT PASS`/`VERDICT FAIL`; a bare `PASS` written by `assert.sh`
before later checks of the same case is only evidence, not a verdict), and refuses to start
if any preceding passing evidence is missing:

```bash
BOOT_GUARD_START_CASE=7 \
CPU_KUBECONFIG="${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" \
NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE}" \
CPU_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER="${CPU_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER}" \
AWS_REGION="${AWS_REGION}" \
RUN_DIR="${RUN_DIR}" \
PYTHON=.venv/bin/python \
  bash scripts/e2e/regional/run_regional_boot_guard_cases.sh \
  --run-dir "${RUN_DIR}" --plan
```

When resuming from BOOT-008, change the value above to `8`. A resume also regenerates and
reviews the plan for that starting point first, then executes with the same
`BOOT_GUARD_START_CASE` and environment; the approval of an old starting point cannot be
used to skip ahead.

The runner still calls the repository fixture above and deletes the probe, the temporary
Secret and the separate database in an EXIT trap; it does not lower any guard or modify the
production Deployment.

**Why the verdict cannot use `rollout status`**: the `startupProbe` is
`failureThreshold=120 × periodSeconds=5` = 600 seconds, so `rollout status`
would idle for 10 minutes before failing. `assert.sh` polls Pod status and logs instead.

**`reset.sh` is mandatory between cases; neither a `set env` rolling update nor
`delete --wait=true` alone is acceptable.** `reset.sh` must wait until the count of Pods
with the same label reaches zero; `assert.sh` must accept exactly one Pod and refuse to
judge as soon as it sees more than one.

Cleanup chain after the whole group (implemented by `cleanup.sh`, re-check item by item):
delete the probe Deployment (and wait for Pods to reach zero) → delete
`gpu-fault-aurora-guardprobe` and the per-case temporary Secrets →
`DROP DATABASE gpu_fault_guardprobe` (requires an explicit `--drop-database`; three
protections: assert the current connection is the production database, assert the target ≠
the current database, skip if it does not exist) → re-check that production
`generation`/`readyReplicas` match the P1 record and that no probe appears in the endpoints →
`shred -u` the local temporary files.

The verdict for every case is uniform: **the Pod enters `CrashLoopBackOff` or `Error`, and
the specified `RuntimeError` text appears in the log**.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-001

**Regional mode without a cluster registry must fail to start**

- Purpose: when `GPU_FAULT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE=regional` but
  `GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON` is not provided, the control plane must not run in a
  "zero managed clusters" state.
- Code basis:
  `src/gpu_fault/settings.py::ControlPlaneSettings.from_mapping`
  (`if regional_mode:` →
  `if not raw_clusters: raise RuntimeError(...)`; the error text is split across lines 398
  and 399 by implicit string concatenation, so **a single-line `grep` cannot find the whole
  sentence**; search by prefix when checking).
- Steps (complete P1~P6 of §4.0 first):
  1. Generate this case's manifest and apply it:

     ```bash
     python3 mutate.py del GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON \
       | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
     ```
  2. `./assert.sh 'regional mode requires GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON'`
  3. Additionally confirm that `/healthz` never returned 200:

     ```bash
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get endpoints gpu-fault-api \
       -o jsonpath='{range .subsets[*].addresses[*]}{.targetRef.name}{"\n"}{end}'
     ```

     No `gpu-fault-api-guard-probe-*` may appear in the output
     (this verifies both that the guard works and that the §4.0 risk-1 isolation is really
     in place).
- Verdict:
  - The Pod must **not** be Ready;
  - the log contains `regional mode requires GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON`;
  - the probe is not in the endpoints of any production Service.
- Meaning of failure: the control plane may accept data-plane requests with no cluster
  registered at all, which amounts to switching off the entire cluster isolation layer.
  **Blocks go-live.**
- Cleanup: `./reset.sh` (deletes the probe and waits for Pods to reach zero).

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-002

**An invalid registry must fail to start; an explicit empty list must stay healthy**

- Code basis:
  `src/gpu_fault/settings.py::ControlPlaneSettings.from_mapping`.
  A missing variable is still rejected by `BOOT-001`; an explicit `[]` is the legitimate
  "no managed GPU clusters at present" steady state, used to keep the CPU control plane
  after the last GPU cluster is deregistered.
- Steps: run one round for each of the three bad inputs and one for the legitimate empty
  list; **the probe must be deleted between rounds** (see false-green trap two in §4.0).

  ```bash
  for payload in '{"cluster_id":' '{}' '[1]'; do
    echo "===== payload: ${payload}"
    ./reset.sh
    kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
      create secret generic gpu-fault-regional-clusters-bad \
      --from-literal=clusters.json="${payload}" \
      --dry-run=client -o yaml \
      | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
    python3 mutate.py sref GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON \
      gpu-fault-regional-clusters-bad clusters.json \
      | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
    if [[ "${payload}" == '{"cluster_id":' ]]; then
      ./assert.sh 'GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON is invalid'
    elif [[ "${payload}" == '{}' ]]; then
      ./assert.sh 'regional cluster registry must be a list'
    else
      ./assert.sh 'regional cluster registry entries must be objects'
    fi
  done
  ```

  Then write `[]` separately; the probe must become Ready. From inside the probe, request
  `GET /v1/regional/clusters` with `GPU_FAULT_EXECUTION_TOKEN`; it must return
  `HTTP 200` and an empty array.
- Verdict: truncated JSON, a non-array object, and an array containing non-object elements
  all fail to start; an explicit `[]` starts successfully and the administrator cluster list
  is empty.
- Cleanup: delete the probe and the `gpu-fault-regional-clusters-bad` Secret.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-003

**Regional mode and the single-cluster variable are mutually exclusive**

- Purpose: the regional control plane must never treat "the EKS it runs on" as a managed
  GPU cluster.
- Code basis:
  `src/gpu_fault/settings.py::ControlPlaneSettings.from_mapping`.
- **Current order**: this guard runs in `Settings.from_mapping()`, before the store is
  constructed and before the registry upsert, so this case writes neither the production
  database nor the probe database. The separate database must still be kept, because the
  later BOOT-004/005/006/009 get past settings and persist the registry.
- Steps:
  1. While keeping a valid `GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON`, the probe additionally sets
     `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER=<cpu-control-plane>`
     (**deliberately the control plane's own HyperPod name, which is exactly the most
     dangerous misconfiguration**):

     ```bash
     ./reset.sh
     python3 mutate.py set GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER \
       <cpu-control-plane> \
       | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
     ./assert.sh \
       'regional mode uses the cluster registry; GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER must be unset'
     ```
- Verdict: the log contains
  `regional mode uses the cluster registry; GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER must be unset`;
  the Pod is not Ready.
- Meaning of failure: the control plane's CPU nodes could be rebooted or replaced by their
  own GPU-fault workflow.
  **Blocks go-live.**

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-004

**Regional mode forbids the in-cluster Kubernetes adapter**

- Code basis:
  `src/gpu_fault/settings.py::ControlPlaneSettings.from_mapping`
  (raises in regional mode when `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_KUBERNETES_ADAPTER` is `true`).
- Steps:

  ```bash
  ./reset.sh
  python3 mutate.py set GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_KUBERNETES_ADAPTER true \
    | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
  ./assert.sh \
    'regional control plane must not enable the in-cluster KubernetesWorkflowAdapter'
  ```

  In the source the expected text is assembled from two lines,
  `"regional control plane must not enable the " "in-cluster KubernetesWorkflowAdapter"`,
  but at runtime it is one sentence; `assert.sh` matches the whole sentence with
  `grep -F`, which is correct.
- Verdict: the log contains
  `regional control plane must not enable the in-cluster KubernetesWorkflowAdapter`.
- Meaning of failure: the control plane would use its own in-cluster ServiceAccount to
  cordon/drain/delete Pods, targeting the control-plane EKS instead of the GPU cluster.
  **Blocks go-live.**

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-005

**Regional mode forbids the central HyperPod mutation adapter**

- Code basis:
  `src/gpu_fault/settings.py::ControlPlaneSettings.from_mapping`
  (regional mode forbids enabling the central HyperPod adapter).
- Steps:

  ```bash
  ./reset.sh
  python3 mutate.py set GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_ADAPTER true \
    | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
  ./assert.sh \
    'regional control plane must delegate HyperPod mutations to the target cluster executor'
  ```
- Verdict: the log contains
  `regional control plane must delegate HyperPod mutations to the target cluster executor`.
- Additional assertion: while this probe is attempting to start, use CloudTrail to confirm
  that **no**
  `RebootClusterNodes` / `BatchDeleteClusterNodes` / `BatchReplaceClusterNodes`
  call originated from the control-plane Pod's role.

  The mutation verbs must be enumerated; do not use `contains(EventName, 'ClusterNodes')`,
  which would mix read-only calls such as `ListClusterNodes` into the result.

  ```bash
  aws cloudtrail lookup-events --region "${AWS_REGION}" \
    --start-time "$(date -u -d '25 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=sagemaker.amazonaws.com \
    --query 'Events[?EventName==`RebootClusterNodes` || EventName==`BatchDeleteClusterNodes` || EventName==`BatchReplaceClusterNodes` || EventName==`UpdateClusterSoftware`].[EventTime,EventName,Username]' \
    --output json
  ```

  Verdict: the output is `[]`. To also confirm that those read-only calls were not issued
  by the control plane:

  ```bash
  aws cloudtrail lookup-events --region "${AWS_REGION}" \
    --start-time "$(date -u -d '25 minutes ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=sagemaker.amazonaws.com \
    --query 'Events[?EventName==`ListClusterNodes`].Username' --output json \
    | python3 -c 'import json,sys;from collections import Counter;
[print(v,"x",k) for k,v in Counter(json.load(sys.stdin)).items()]'
  ```

  Verdict: the role corresponding to the control-plane Pod Identity must **not** appear
  among the callers.

  When `run_regional_boot_guard_cases.sh` performs this step and `CONTROL_PLANE_ROLE_NAME`
  is exported, it keeps only events whose `Username` contains that role name (the evidence
  records `cloudtrail_filter=role:<name>`; if not exported it records
  `cloudtrail_filter=none`). The query happens within minutes of the probe start, inside the
  15-minute CloudTrail delivery window, so the evidence always records
  `cloudtrail_provisional=true`; the final re-check of this provisional conclusion is done
  by `DESTR-013`, whose CloudTrail query covers all destructive phases.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-006

**Retired**: this guard (`regional control plane cannot run in-cluster
quick diagnostics against its own EKS`) was removed together with the quick diagnostics
path; `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_QUICK_DIAGNOSTICS` no longer exists, and this case is no longer
executed and produces no evidence.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-007

**Lower bound on cluster token length**

- Purpose: a token in the registry must be at least 32 characters; a short token must not
  register successfully.
- Code basis: `src/gpu_fault/regional.py::cluster_token_sha256` (`cluster_token_sha256`
  raises `ValueError` when `len(token) < 32`),
  called from
  `src/gpu_fault/settings.py::ControlPlaneSettings.from_mapping`.
  **Note that it raises `ValueError`, not `RuntimeError`**,
  but the verdict looks only at the log text, not at the exception type.
- Steps (one negative and one positive branch; the registry uses the production shape but
  with a fake cluster id, to avoid a key collision with the production registry):

  `registry.py` (in `scripts/e2e/regional/boot_guard/`) generates the registry JSON:
  the field shape matches production, but `cluster_id` is replaced by
  `guardprobe-fake-cluster` so that it does not collide with a production registry key;
  the token is the predictable `"g" * n`, because BOOT-008 branch 3 needs it to fire one
  data-plane request itself and verify the 403. The fixture must also supply a non-empty
  `agent_endpoint_allowed_cidrs`, otherwise the current registry schema rejects the entry
  first and the token-length guard this case verifies is never reached. That value is fixed
  to RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 `192.0.2.0/24`; never fill in a private range that could overlap
  a real VPC.

  ```bash
  probe_registry () {   # $1..$4 are passed through to registry.py
    ./reset.sh || return 1        # must wait for Pods to reach zero; delete --wait alone is not enough
    kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
      create secret generic gpu-fault-regional-clusters-probe \
      --from-literal=clusters.json="$(python3 registry.py "$@")" \
      --dry-run=client -o yaml \
      | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
    python3 mutate.py sref GPU_FAULT_REGIONAL_CLUSTERS_JSON \
      gpu-fault-regional-clusters-probe clusters.json \
      | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
  }
  ```

  1. Negative (31 characters):

     ```bash
     probe_registry 31
     ./assert.sh 'cluster token must contain at least 32 characters'
     ```
  2. Positive (32 characters, expected Ready) -- `assert.sh` **cannot** be used here,
     because its verdict is "not Ready". Wait for Ready instead:

     ```bash
     probe_registry 32
     PROBE_POD="$(kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get pod -l app="${PROBE}" -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')"
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       wait --for=condition=ready pod/"${PROBE_POD}" --timeout=600s
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get pod "${PROBE_POD}" \
       -o custom-columns=READY:.status.containerStatuses[0].ready,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount \
       --no-headers
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       logs "${PROBE_POD}" --tail=200 \
       | grep -c 'cluster token must contain' || echo "no token error (expected)"
     ```

     `--timeout=600s` is used because the `startupProbe` allows 600 seconds
     (`failureThreshold=120 × periodSeconds=5`),
     and the first start also has to `pip install` the wheel.

     Wait for `condition=ready` on the specific Pod; do not substitute the Deployment's
     `condition=available` for Pod readiness.

     Another observation trap: if the negative branch has just run before this step,
     `get pod -l` may also list **the old Pod that is still terminating**, making it look
     as if `replicas=1` yet there are 2 Pods, both `ready=false`. `probe_registry` already
     runs `reset.sh` first and waits for Pods to reach zero, so this does not occur when
     the commands are executed in the order above; but if you run single commands by hand,
     remember to confirm first that `get pod -l app="${PROBE}"` shows only one line.
- Verdict: 31 fails, 32 succeeds; the boundary is exact.
- Cleanup: delete the probe and the `gpu-fault-regional-clusters-probe` Secret.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-008

**Registry field integrity and the semantics of `enabled=false`**

- Code basis: `src/gpu_fault/regional.py::RegionalClusterRegistration`
  (`RegionalClusterRegistration(StrictModel)`; `StrictModel` in
  `src/gpu_fault/models.py::StrictModel` sets `extra="forbid"`, so unknown fields are
  rejected; `authenticates()` requires `self.enabled` at `49-53`).
- Steps (reuse the `probe_registry` function defined in BOOT-007):
  1. Missing `eks_cluster_arn`:

     ```bash
     probe_registry 64 "" eks_cluster_arn
     ./assert.sh 'validation error for RegionalClusterRegistration'
     ```

     The log will show both `eks_cluster_arn` and `Field required`;
     `BOOT-017` step 3 has already seen the shape of this error on live hardware (all
     missing fields listed at once).
  2. Misspelled field `alowed_namespaces` (one `l` short):

     ```bash
     probe_registry 64 "" "" alowed_namespaces
     ./assert.sh 'Extra inputs are not permitted'
     ```

     **This one matters especially**: if a misspelled allowlist field name were silently
     ignored, `allowed_namespaces` would degrade to the default empty list and the
     namespace gate would exist in name only.
  3. `"enabled": false`: the probe should become **Ready normally**, but that cluster's
     credential is rejected. The token is known (`registry.py` uses `"g" * 64`),
     so a data-plane request can be fired directly from inside the probe Pod:

     ```bash
     probe_registry 64 disabled
     PROBE_POD="$(kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get pod -l app="${PROBE}" -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')"
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       wait --for=condition=ready pod/"${PROBE_POD}" --timeout=600s
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       exec -i "${PROBE_POD}" -- python - <<'PY'
     import json, urllib.error, urllib.request
     req = urllib.request.Request(
         "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/regional/executors/claim",
         data=json.dumps({
             "executor_id": "boot008-disabled-probe",
             "executor_protocol_version": 2,
             "execution_owners": ["gpu-fault-kubernetes-adapter"],
             "max_commands": 1,
             "lease_seconds": 60,
         }).encode(),
         headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                  "X-GPU-Fault-Cluster-ID": "guardprobe-fake-cluster",
                  "Authorization": "Bearer " + "g" * 64},
         method="POST")
     try:
         with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as r:
             print("UNEXPECTED", r.status, r.read()[:200])
     except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
         print("status", e.code, e.read()[:200])
     PY
     ```

     A route that really exists and is declared as `cluster-token` must be used. An older
     version of this document wrote `/v1/gpu-events/guardprobe-fake-cluster`; that path
     matches no GPU event handler and is simply rejected by default-deny as
     `no declared authorization bucket`, so it cannot test `enabled=false` at all.

     Expect `status 403` with detail
     `regional cluster authentication failed`
     (`src/gpu_fault/app/`: `authenticates()` returns `False` because of
     `enabled=False`, taking the "authentication failed" branch rather than the
     "not registered" one --
     do **not** expect `regional cluster is not registered`, which is the text for a
     cluster_id that cannot be found).
- Verdict: the behaviour of the three cases matches the above; case 3 must be a 403 with
  the Pod Ready.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-009

**Dependency gate of the managed recovery observer**

- Code basis:
  `src/gpu_fault/app/context.py::ApplicationContext._managed_observer`
  (raises when `enable_managed_observer` is true and `context.fleet_registry is None`);
  note that the second guard in the same function
  (`ENABLE_KUBERNETES_ADAPTER=true`) is short-circuited by
  `not context.regional_mode` on line `697` and **does not apply to this deployment
  shape**; do not mistake it for an assertion that should fire.
- Precondition reminder: production already has
  `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_MANAGED_OBSERVER=true`
  and `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY=true` (a legitimate combination);
  this case only flips the latter to `false`, i.e. a **single-variable** mutation.
- Steps:

  ```bash
  ./reset.sh
  python3 mutate.py set GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY false \
    | kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" apply -f -
  ./assert.sh \
    'HyperPod managed recovery observer requires GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY=true'
  ```
- Verdict: the log contains
  `HyperPod managed recovery observer requires GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY=true`.

### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-010

**The three production replicas started correctly in regional mode**

- Purpose: all of the above are negative cases; this one is the positive gate: confirm that
  the three replicas actually serving are indeed in regional mode and that the **four
  dangerous switches that "must be false"** are indeed off.
- Exact expectation list:

  | Variable | Expected | Notes |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `GPU_FAULT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE` | `regional` | Regional mode itself |
  | `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_KUBERNETES_ADAPTER` | `false` | Corresponds to BOOT-004 |
  | `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_ADAPTER` | `false` | Corresponds to BOOT-005 |
  | `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_NODE_ACTION_ADAPTER` | `false` | Node actions must be delegated too |
  | `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_SPARE_FAILOVER` | `false` | Warm-spare failover belongs to the executor |
  | `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_HYPERPOD_MANAGED_OBSERVER` | **`true`** | **Not a dangerous switch**; it only observes, and the BOOT-009 guard requires `ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY=true` alongside it |
  | `GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY` | **`true`** | Same as above, the legitimate precondition of BOOT-009 |
  | `GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER` | **absent** | Corresponds to BOOT-003 |
  | `GPU_FAULT_PROCESSOR_MODE` | `active-active` | The three replicas consume concurrently |

- Steps:
  1. Read the environment variables actually in effect (from inside the Pods, not from the
     manifest):

     ```bash
     for pod in $(kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
         get pod -l app=gpu-fault-api-ha -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
       echo "== ${pod}"
       kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
         exec "${pod}" -- printenv \
         | grep -E '^GPU_FAULT_(DEPLOYMENT_MODE|ENABLE_KUBERNETES_ADAPTER|ENABLE_NODE_ACTION_ADAPTER|ENABLE_HYPERPOD_ADAPTER|ENABLE_HYPERPOD_SPARE_FAILOVER|ENABLE_HYPERPOD_MANAGED_OBSERVER|ENABLE_AGENT_REGISTRY|ENABLE_QUICK_DIAGNOSTICS|HYPERPOD_CLUSTER|PROCESSOR_MODE)=' \
         | sort
     done
     ```
  2. Confirm that the output of the three replicas is **identical** and matches the
     expectation list above line by line.
     Three-replica consistency is compared through a digest of the normalised output; the
     concrete digest value changes with the release, and the only requirement is that the
     three running replicas agree.
  3. Confirm that the registry is loaded: `cp_get /v1/regional/clusters` requires
     `X-GPU-Fault-Execution-Token`, so use the read-only side channel instead --
     for every `CLUSTER_ID`, `cp_get "/v1/collector-status/${CLUSTER_ID}"` returns 200
     (rather than 404/500). `run_regional_boot_guard_cases.sh` requests this side channel
     from inside one API Pod for every registered `cluster_id`; any non-200 is FAIL, and
     the result is written into the evidence.
  4. Confirm that the three replicas are spread over three different CPU nodes:

     ```bash
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get pod -l app=gpu-fault-api-ha \
       -o custom-columns=POD:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName
     ```
- Verdict: the three replicas' environment variables agree, all six guard conditions are
  met, and the three replicas land on three different nodes.
- Meaning of failure: the manifest and the actual runtime disagree (for example the Secret
  was not rolled, or an old ReplicaSet lingers), and the conclusions of every subsequent
  case are untrustworthy. **Fix this first before continuing.**


#### Structural gaps that remain in this group

`BOOT-001` ~ `BOOT-010` are all "configuration validation at the instant of startup".
**Not one of them covers time-delayed failures** (for example "restart after credential
rotation" or "a Secret modified while running"). Such failures do not surface at startup,
and the existing guards cannot reach them. Until this is filled in, a PASS for this group can
only claim "the configuration is safe at startup time".
### GF-REGIONAL-BOOT-011

**Secret key completeness of the data-plane executor manifest (greenfield deployability)**

- Purpose: `BOOT-001` ~ `BOOT-010` only prove "refuses to start when the configuration is unsafe";
  they do not prove "following the documentation once actually brings it up". This case is the
  **first gate of a first-time deployment**: every `secretKeyRef` referenced by the executor
  Deployment must actually be created by a step in `docs/en/deployment-and-operations-manual.md`.
- Code basis: `deploy/dataplane/cluster-action-executor.yaml:84-174`
  lists all `secretKeyRef`s; `REG-4. Create the connection Secret on the GPU EKS` in
  `docs/en/deployment-and-operations-manual.md` §5.3 is the only step that creates
  `gpu-fault-regional-connection`.
- Isolation requirement: this case must connect to the isolated control plane created by `BOOT-016` and use a separate
  `TEST_CLUSTER_ID`/token/namespace. Reusing the production cluster ID and token is forbidden;
  otherwise the temporary Executor would take part in production command claims and this case would no longer be a deployability check.
- Steps:
  1. Mechanically compute the set difference between the keys the manifest requires and the keys actually created; **do not rely on eyeballing**.
     The manifest is 5 YAML documents (ServiceAccount / ClusterRole /
     ClusterRoleBinding / Deployment, plus a trailing empty document),
     so you must use `safe_load_all` and then filter out the Deployment --
     `safe_load` only reads the first ServiceAccount and fails with `KeyError`.
     Also print the optional items, to confirm that "the manual does not create it" is intentional rather than an omission:

     ```bash
     cd <repository-root>
     python3 - <<'PY'
     import re, yaml
     doc = open("docs/部署和运维手册.md").read()
     docs = list(yaml.safe_load_all(
         open("deploy/dataplane/cluster-action-executor.yaml")))
     man = [d for d in docs if d and d.get("kind") == "Deployment"][0]
     required, optional = [], []
     for c in man["spec"]["template"]["spec"]["containers"]:
         for e in c.get("env", []):
             ref = (e.get("valueFrom") or {}).get("secretKeyRef")
             if not ref:
                 continue
             (optional if ref.get("optional") else required).append(
                 (ref["name"], ref["key"], e["name"]))
     missing = 0
     for name, key, env in sorted(set(required)):
         created = re.search(rf"--from-(file|literal)={re.escape(key)}=", doc)
         if not created:
             missing += 1
         print(f"{'OK     ' if created else 'MISSING'} {name}/{key} -> {env}")
     print("--- optional (the manual is not required to create these) ---")
     for name, key, env in sorted(set(optional)):
         created = re.search(rf"--from-(file|literal)={re.escape(key)}=", doc)
         print(f"{'OK     ' if created else 'ABSENT '} {name}/{key} -> {env}")
     print(f"\nMISSING_COUNT={missing}")
     PY
     ```
  2. For every `MISSING` item, confirm on the real GPU cluster that the key really does not exist:

     ```bash
     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get secret gpu-fault-regional-connection \
       -o jsonpath='{.data}' | python3 -c \
       'import json,sys; print(sorted(json.load(sys.stdin)))'
     ```
  3. In a **brand-new namespace**, execute steps 3~5 of `docs/en/deployment-and-operations-manual.md` exactly as written,
     then run `kubectl describe pod` to see the container creation result.

     The Secret material must be **derived from the source**; do not copy an existing object with
     `kubectl get secret -o yaml` -- copying tests "whether the copy works", whereas this case tests
     "whether the manual's derivation commands are correct". The only exception is `cluster-token`: it cannot be regenerated,
     otherwise it would not match the `token_sha256` in the control-plane registry,
     and the failure reason would become 401 instead of the missing key this case is meant to test.

     ```bash
     export TEST_NS=gf-boot011
     export ALLOWED_NAMESPACES=training

     # Manual step 3: the master is used only on the trusted deploy host for derivation; it is never written into the GPU Secret
     kubectl --kubeconfig "${CPU_KUBECONFIG}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get secret gpu-fault-control-plane-active \
       -o jsonpath='{.data.node-action-secret}' |
       base64 -d > "${SECURE_DIR}/node-action-secret"
     chmod 0600 "${SECURE_DIR}/node-action-secret"

     export NLB_PKI_SECRET_ID=gpu-fault/regional-control-plane/nlb-private-pki
     aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --region "${AWS_REGION}" \
       --secret-id "${NLB_PKI_SECRET_ID}" --query SecretString --output text |
       jq -r .ca_certificate > "${SECURE_DIR}/control-plane-ca.crt"
     chmod 0644 "${SECURE_DIR}/control-plane-ca.crt"
     openssl x509 -in "${SECURE_DIR}/control-plane-ca.crt" -noout \
       -subject -issuer -dates

     # The only material that must be reused
     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
       get secret gpu-fault-regional-connection \
       -o jsonpath='{.data.cluster-token}' |
       base64 -d > "${SECURE_DIR}/cluster-token"
     chmod 0600 "${SECURE_DIR}/cluster-token"
     ```

     Execute manual step 4 verbatim, but **deliberately do not create** `node-agent-endpoints` --
     this is exactly the core assertion of this case: the manual never creates it,
     so the manifest must tolerate its absence via `optional: true`.

     ```bash
     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" create namespace "${TEST_NS}"

     printf '%s' "${CONTROL_PLANE_URL}"     > "${SECURE_DIR}/control-plane-url"
     printf '%s' "${CLUSTER_ID}"            > "${SECURE_DIR}/cluster-id"
     printf '%s' "${ALLOWED_NAMESPACES}"    > "${SECURE_DIR}/allowed-namespaces"
     printf '%s' "${HYPERPOD_CLUSTER_NAME}" > "${SECURE_DIR}/hyperpod-cluster-name"
     printf '%s' "${HYPERPOD_CLUSTER_NAME}" > "${SECURE_DIR}/hyperpod-confirm-cluster-name"

     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${TEST_NS}" \
       create secret generic gpu-fault-regional-connection \
       --from-file=control-plane-url="${SECURE_DIR}/control-plane-url" \
       --from-file=cluster-id="${SECURE_DIR}/cluster-id" \
       --from-file=cluster-token="${SECURE_DIR}/cluster-token" \
       --from-file=allowed-namespaces="${SECURE_DIR}/allowed-namespaces" \
       --from-file=hyperpod-cluster-name="${SECURE_DIR}/hyperpod-cluster-name" \
       --from-file=hyperpod-confirm-cluster-name="${SECURE_DIR}/hyperpod-confirm-cluster-name" \
       --from-file=ca.crt="${SECURE_DIR}/control-plane-ca.crt" \
       --dry-run=client -o yaml |
     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" apply -f -

     GPU_FAULT_KUBECTL_CONTEXT="${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" \
     GPU_FAULT_NAMESPACE="${TEST_NS}" \
     GPU_FAULT_CLUSTER_ID="${CLUSTER_ID}" \
     GPU_FAULT_HYPERPOD_CLUSTER="${HYPERPOD_CLUSTER_NAME}" \
     GPU_FAULT_FLEET_MASTER_FILE="${SECURE_DIR}/node-action-secret" \
       deploy/node/provision-node-action-keys.sh
     ```

     The test namespace must use a separate least-privilege test IRSA role whose trust contains only
     `system:serviceaccount:${TEST_NS}:gpu-fault-cluster-executor`.
     Modifying the trust policy of the production Executor role for this case is forbidden, and a wildcard namespace must not be used.

     Replacing only the ConfigMap name in manual step 5 is still **not enough**: in the manifest
     `namespace: gpu-fault-system` is hard-coded in 3 places, and
     `ClusterRole`/`ClusterRoleBinding` are **cluster-scoped resources with the same names**,
     so applying directly would overwrite the production RBAC. They must be renamed for isolation as well:

     ```bash
     export WHEEL="$(
       jq -r '.components.executor.wheel' dist/current-release.json
     )"
     export ARTIFACT_SHA256="$(
       jq -r '.components.executor.wheel_sha256' dist/current-release.json
     )"
     export COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST="$(
       jq -r '.components.executor.module_digest' dist/current-release.json
     )"
     export WHEEL_CONFIG_MAP="gpu-fault-executor-wheel-0100-${ARTIFACT_SHA256:0:12}"
     export EXECUTOR_IRSA_ROLE_ARN="$(
       kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${NAMESPACE}" \
         get serviceaccount gpu-fault-cluster-executor \
         -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.eks\.amazonaws\.com/role-arn}'
     )"
     test -n "${EXECUTOR_IRSA_ROLE_ARN}"

     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${TEST_NS}" \
       create configmap "${WHEEL_CONFIG_MAP}" --from-file="${WHEEL}"

     WHEEL_CONFIG_MAP="${WHEEL_CONFIG_MAP}" \
     EXECUTOR_IRSA_ROLE_ARN="${EXECUTOR_IRSA_ROLE_ARN}" \
     ARTIFACT_SHA256="${ARTIFACT_SHA256}" \
     COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST="${COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST}" \
     AWS_REGION="${AWS_REGION}" TEST_NS="${TEST_NS}" \
     python3 - <<'PY'
     import os, yaml

     src = "/tmp/gf-e2e/boot011-executor.yaml"
     docs = [
         item
         for item in yaml.safe_load_all(
             open("deploy/dataplane/cluster-action-executor.yaml")
         )
         if item
     ]
     replacements = {
         "REPLACE_WITH_EXECUTOR_IRSA_ROLE_ARN":
             os.environ["EXECUTOR_IRSA_ROLE_ARN"],
         "REPLACE_WITH_AWS_REGION": os.environ["AWS_REGION"],
         "REPLACE_WITH_EXECUTOR_ARTIFACT_SHA256":
             os.environ["ARTIFACT_SHA256"],
         "REPLACE_WITH_EXECUTOR_COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST":
             os.environ["COMPATIBILITY_DIGEST"],
     }

     def replace(value):
         if isinstance(value, str):
             for source, target in replacements.items():
                 value = value.replace(source, target)
             return value
         if isinstance(value, list):
             return [replace(item) for item in value]
         if isinstance(value, dict):
             return {key: replace(item) for key, item in value.items()}
         return value

     docs = [replace(item) for item in docs]
     for d in docs:
         if "namespace" in d["metadata"]:
             d["metadata"]["namespace"] = os.environ["TEST_NS"]
         if d["kind"] in {"ClusterRole", "ClusterRoleBinding"}:
             d["metadata"]["name"] += "-boot011"
         if d["kind"] == "ClusterRoleBinding":
             d["roleRef"]["name"] += "-boot011"
             for subject in d["subjects"]:
                 subject["namespace"] = os.environ["TEST_NS"]
         if d["kind"] == "Deployment":
             d["spec"]["replicas"] = 1
             for volume in d["spec"]["template"]["spec"]["volumes"]:
                 if volume["name"] == "artifact":
                     volume["configMap"]["name"] = (
                         os.environ["WHEEL_CONFIG_MAP"]
                     )
     yaml.safe_dump_all(docs, open(src, "w"), sort_keys=False)
     PY

     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" apply -f /tmp/gf-e2e/boot011-executor.yaml
     ```
  4. Verdict commands:

     ```bash
     timeout 200 kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${TEST_NS}" \
       rollout status deployment/gpu-fault-cluster-executor --timeout=180s

     kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" -n "${TEST_NS}" \
       describe pod -l app=gpu-fault-cluster-executor |
       grep -E 'CreateContainerConfigError|couldn.t find key' ||
       echo "none of the above errors"
     ```

     A brief `Startup probe failed` Warning while the wheel is being installed is normal;
     when the Pod ends up Ready with no Secret key/config errors, that Warning must not be judged a failure.
- Verdict:
  - The output of step 1 **must be all `OK`** (`MISSING_COUNT=0`);
  - The Pod of step 3 must be Ready within 180 seconds and must **not** show
    `CreateContainerConfigError` or
    `couldn't find key <key> in Secret`.
- Security assertion: only the test cluster ID may appear in the registry of the isolated control plane; the production control plane's
  `remote_command_total` and Executor logs must not show the test executor ID within this case's window.
- Regression requirement: this case is kept as a standing gate. Any newly added `secretKeyRef`
  must appear at the same time in the Secret creation step of the deployment and operations manual, or be marked `optional: true`;
  the diff script of step 1 is the mechanical check of this constraint.
- Cleanup: delete the temporary namespace **and the two renamed cluster-scoped resources**.
  Deleting only the namespace leaves dangling ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding objects:

  ```bash

  kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" \
    delete clusterrole gpu-fault-cluster-executor-boot011
  kubectl --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}" \
    delete clusterrolebinding gpu-fault-cluster-executor-boot011
  rm -f "${SECURE_DIR}"/{cluster-token,node-action-secret,control-plane-ca.crt,control-plane-url,cluster-id,allowed-namespaces,hyperpod-cluster-name,hyperpod-confirm-cluster-name}
  ```
