     on the ephemeral HostProbe staying alive.
     Only after verifying the recovery timer's actual command, state and fixed deadline does it lower
     the power per UUID.
     The load is constrained by an exclusive systemd cgroup and a timeout with a hard-kill bound, and
     must end before the recovery deadline.
     Before handing over to the load command, the node writes a non-overwritable start receipt bound to
     run, boot, GPU, change digest and UTC/monotonic time; the reporting latency is measured from that
     moment. The remote request and safety-preparation durations are recorded separately; preparation
     time must not be counted as Collector response time, and a later sample time must not be used to
     backfill the starting point.
  3. Poll the GPU chain's `observed_at` once per collection cycle (written to
     `timeline.json` each time) until it changes or the load ends.
     `collector_status` is an overwritable latest state; the polled values serve only as auxiliary
     observation. The anomaly latency is taken from the `ingested_at` of the earliest matching
     persistent DCGM candidate batch in this window, validating cluster/node, batch/record ID, the
     UUID/index of the loaded GPU, the power/utilisation conditions and the collection/ingestion time
     order. Later overwritten states are not treated as the first delivery, and records for unrelated
     GPUs, malformed records or records with future timestamps are not used.
  4. Regardless of the outcome, request `restore-gpu-power-limit`. Without this run's change intent no
     GPU is written, and a rejected custom power limit is not reset to the default. For an existing
     change, first prove that the owning load/cgroup has stopped, then restore the saved baseline over
     the original UUID set and verify per GPU, and only at the end revoke the timer and the unit with
     proven ownership.
     On identity drift, a load that has not stopped or an unknown recovery result, keep the independent
     recovery material and do not record cleanup success.
- Verdict (PASS only if all hold):
  - a new `observed_at` appears after injection;
  - the delivery latency is ≤ `interval x (EDGE_CONFIRMATION_SAMPLES + 1)`
    (in production 15 x (3+1) = 60 seconds, far below the 300-second summary);
  - within the window a `GPU_METRICS` evidence record exists whose `edge_filter_reasons` contains
    candidate / threshold;
  - at wrap-up every GPU's `power.limit` equals `power.default_limit`.
  - the power-lowering receipt explicitly proves that the change, timer and load were established; the
    normal wrap-up receipt explicitly proves that the load stopped, the baseline was restored, the
    timer was revoked and cleanup completed; a PASS cannot rest on the current power reading alone.

#### Why the upper bound is "confirmation samples + 1" and not "two collection cycles"

`_should_deliver` appends `candidate-confirmed` only when
`streak == edge_confirmation_samples`
(`GPU_FAULT_DCGM_EDGE_CONFIRMATION_SAMPLES`, 3 in production).
This is **debouncing by design**: fewer readings than this do not count as an anomaly edge.
So the old upper bound of "two collection cycles" was itself wrong --
it is stricter than the fastest delivery the implementation allows,
and would only turn a correct debounce into a P0.
The honest upper bound is **the one cycle in which the anomaly appears, plus the
`EDGE_CONFIRMATION_SAMPLES` cycles needed for confirmation**;
exceeding it means the edge filter is waiting for its own summary, and that is the P0.

#### ⚠ The P0 caught on the first live execution of this case: the duty-cycle counter suppressed the very fault it was meant to expose

On production H200s `DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_VIOLATION`
**advances at about 1.125e9 ns/s even on a completely idle GPU**,
i.e. converted to microseconds the duty cycle is > 100%.
The consequence is fatal: `_candidate_keys` uses
`violation_duty_cycle_threshold` (0.05) to judge the duty cycle out of bounds,
so **every GPU locks permanently into a confirmed candidate about `EDGE_CONFIRMATION_SAMPLES`
samples after the collector starts**;
and a confirmed candidate is announced only on the transition,
after which real power throttling **can never again produce a delivery edge**.
This is exactly the kind of failure COLLECT-002 guards against, only entering through the counter
instead of the summary phase.

Fix: when the duty cycle > `DUTY_CYCLE_MAX_PLAUSIBLE` (1.05, i.e. one minute of violation cannot
exceed one minute plus sampling skew) it **does not participate in anomaly-edge judgement**,
and a WARNING is emitted once for that device/field.
A counter claiming more violation time than has elapsed shows that on this machine it is not of the
dimension "violation microseconds"; an uninterpretable quantity must not be used to judge faults.
The same path on the analysis side (the thermal violation delta in `_throttle_decision`, escalating
to **DRAIN** after two excursions) received the same plausibility gate --
letting an uninterpretable rate through there would **evict healthy nodes**.

⚠ The power finding path (`gpu_power_policy.power_violation_decision`)
**deliberately does not get this gate**: it already requires the power-limit correlation to hold at
the same time, and adding the gate there would discard true positives.

#### Safety notes

- Lowering the enforced power limit is **reducing heat and power**, not overclocking;
  there is no hardware damage risk; `nvidia-smi -pl` is a reversible operation supported by the driver.
- The load duration and the deadman restore duration are validated by the runner:
  `load_seconds > restore_seconds` raises `ProbeError` outright
  (the load must end before the restore, otherwise the restore lands in the middle of the load).
- It does not touch `NodeRecovery`, performs no replacement, and does not write `/dev/kmsg`.




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-003

**Live verification of `EXPECTED_GPU_COUNT` / `EXPECTED_EFA_DEVICE_COUNT`**

- Formal entry: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_acceptance.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-003`.
- Purpose: misconfiguring these two values (e.g. the cluster moves to 4-GPU machines while 8 remains
  written) causes **constant false positives** or **constant misses**, with no error ever raised.
- Steps:
  1. The host probe reads the number of UUID rows of the actual GPU inventory using
     `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,pci.bus_id,name --format=csv,noheader`,
     without treating MIG description rows or error text as physical GPUs;
     EFA must replicate the implementation's criterion: the driver is `efa` and at least one port has
     `state=4`, `phys_state=5`. A direct
     `ls /sys/class/infiniband | wc -l` is forbidden.
  2. Compare with `/etc/gpu-fault/collector.env`, and verify through `inventory-config` that the
     running host collector's numeric whitelist configuration is identical; bind PID/start
     ticks/InvocationID and the file digest, fail if the process or file changes during the read, and
     output no other environment or credentials.
  3. Read, for the exact cluster/node, the four latest GPU/EFA expected/active metrics and the
     mismatch signal state; the counts agree and missing/excess/consecutive are all zero, there is a
     fresh successful HOST_TELEMETRY delivery for the node, and the current signal is inactive.
     The Store optimisation allows a never-active signal to be explicitly reported as having no
     record, but the fresh healthy metric proof must hold at the same time; a missing query result,
     stale samples, another node/producer or an active signal cannot PASS.
- Verdict: the three agree (actual = configured = no false positives).
  Any disagreement is a configuration defect.
- ⚠ **This case must be rerun after every instance-type change**;
  it is a pure configuration consistency check, extremely cheap, yet it covers a whole class of silent
  failures.

#### ⚠ The EFA count must not be a direct count of `/sys/class/infiniband/`

`ls /sys/class/infiniband/ | wc -l` is **the wrong method**.
The actual criterion of `src/gpu_fault/collectors/ _efa_inventory` has three layers:

1. `_is_efa_device` (`:2135`) --
   the name the `device/driver` symlink points to must be `efa`,
   or `device/uevent` contains `DRIVER=efa`
   → yields `discovered_count`;
2. for every EFA device iterate `ports/*`,
   requiring some port with
   first field of `state` `== "4"` **and** first field of `phys_state` `== "5"`
   (a missing `phys_state` file is treated as `"5"`)
   → yields `observed_count` (i.e. `active_count`);
3. `missing = max(0, expected - observed)`,
   `excess = max(0, observed - expected)`.

So the live verification script must **replicate these three layers**,
otherwise a machine with a non-EFA RDMA card mixed in would reach a false "consistent" conclusion
(the unit test `test_efa_inventory_ignores_non_efa_rdma_devices`
 protects exactly this direction).




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-004

**Live verification of the `INVENTORY_MISMATCH_CONSECUTIVE_SAMPLES=2` debounce**

- Formal entry: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_destructive.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-004`.
  `--debounce-tolerance` (default `0.5`): the upper bound on the ratio by which the interval from the
  first anomalous sample to the threshold sample may exceed
  `(required_samples - 1) x sampling period`.
- Purpose: this value decides how many consecutive sampling cycles a "GPU drop-off" needs before it is
  reported. Setting it to 1 turns transient jitter into an alert storm,
  setting it too high delays the discovery of a real drop-off.
- Steps: in the **maintenance window** start an independent Host Collector sampling instance with only
  the GPU inventory contributor enabled, using an expected count of `baseline+1`. This instance uses a
  private sink with no network access and no outbox writes; the production `collector.env` and the
  Host Collector service stay unchanged.
  The same sampling process exits after completing two real sampling cycles; batch 1 must carry only
  `consecutive_mismatch_samples=1` and produce no finding, batch 2 must be 2 and produce a finding.
  The runner validates and saves the raw text of these two batches, binds the event IDs, and then
  delivers each once, in the original order, through the real `HttpEventSink` on the node. The control
  plane must persist the identical batches and then execute a real reboot workflow.
  This is a controlled inventory-policy stimulus, not a real GPU drop-off; a successful isolated sample
  is not by itself a live case pass.
- Verdict:
  - the first batch has mismatch value 0, counter 1 and the `baseline` of the restarted collector;
    only the threshold batch is 1, with the counter exactly the configured N. There are N-1 intervals
    from the first batch to the threshold batch, computed from the two batches' collector observed_at;
    the runner start/config change time cannot stand in for the first batch;
    startup spread, service restart and transport time are not part of this sampling interval;
  - the raw evidence is bounded by the host baseline time and matches the exact cluster/node, node
    producer and this run's `expected=baseline+1`. A missing first batch, missing threshold, counter
    regression/restart, mismatched configuration or malformed times all fail;
  - after injection the node has **exactly one** workflow, and the `RESTART_NODE` workflow is `SUCCEEDED`;
  - the two raw batches in the isolated sink agree with the control plane's persistent evidence; the
    publish response alone cannot prove they were processed;
  - the sha256 of the production `collector.env` matches the baseline before and after sampling and
    after the reboot;
  - after the node reboot DCGM and the formal restore complete, and all self-owned probe resources are
    cleaned up.
- When the runner judges "was `RESTART_NODE` planned", it looks at **the node's whole workflow chain
  after injection**, not the latest one. The verdict still requires **exactly one workflow for the node
  after injection**; the appearance of a second workflow is a FAIL.
  The new path no longer overwrites the production configuration, so it does not depend on "restoring
  the expected count in time during the reboot" for the verification to converge.
  Note that the `VALIDATE_GPU` parameters of the `RESTART_NODE` workflow freeze the expected value at
  injection time (baseline+1); the validation adapter caps it at the physical GPU count from the
  instance-type inventory (step details record `inventory_requirement_clamped`), otherwise an 8-GPU
  node could never pass expected=9 and a configuration error would escalate into replace-after and a
  support incident.
  When the DCGM exporter Pod is not yet ready after the reboot, the metrics collector's scrape failures
  are not reported within the `GPU_FAULT_DCGM_STARTUP_GRACE_SECONDS` grace period, otherwise every
  reboot could add a dcgm-fields diagnostic workflow, equally breaking "exactly one".
  A publish response lost at the start of the reboot must not be republished either: the runner uses
  the batch IDs and event IDs saved before publishing to query the persistent evidence, then checks
  the workflow, commands and submission scope. A missing batch, mismatched identity or an explicit
  refusal still fail; an empty response or Ready=True alone does not constitute success.
  Within a fixed, non-renewable 30-minute wait budget the runner repeatedly checks the original Node
  UID and rebuilds the probe only after confirming the new boot is Ready. A changed production file
  digest, extra workflows or cleanup failures are kept as FAIL.
- Layered development verification:
  - `make collect004-check`: the real Collector with an isolated sink, exact batch validation and a
    local workflow-transport stand-in; does not connect to the production control plane, modify the
    host configuration or trigger a reboot.
  - `make collector-recovery-check`: independently verifies the old configuration recovery protocol,
    response loss, ownership and cross-boot state boundaries; these fixture checks do not count as a
    COLLECT-004 live PASS.
  - `make collector-platform-check`: explicitly runs the process/mount boundary checks in a
    host-exclusive user-systemd transient service and a read-only, network-less Docker container. It
    needs a usable user systemd manager, Docker and the local `python:3.12.14-slim` image; missing
    prerequisites fail outright without auto-installing or skipping.
    This check does not reboot the host and is not a physical cross-reboot acceptance.
  - Only then run the checked live entry above; local layered results cannot replace the real
    workflow, provider and cleanup evidence.
- Compatibility with old runs:
  - existing override journals are still cleaned up by their original owner, nonce, digest and
    recovery protocol; old intents must not be rewritten, old guards must not be relaxed, and
    historical filesystem UUIDs must not be fabricated. The new COLLECT-004 no longer creates such node
    records, backups, timers or recovery services.
- Fault ownership and wrap-up:
  - query the incident by the event ID of the real threshold batch, validating cluster, single node,
    creation time, workflow and remote command identity; recovery authority is not obtained via "the
    most recent node workflow".
  - wait timeouts, probe exceptions or interruptions still save this run's operations, known workflows
    and recovery failures. At the end re-read the exactly correlated recovery state; when the
    configuration is not restored, the action has not settled or the read fails, keep an explicit
    manual-reconciliation state, and do not treat the probe Pod deletion or the SQL terminal state as
    node recovery success.
  - when the node guard refuses, after re-verifying ownership save an independent, create-only,
    never-overwritten private failure receipt recording the error code, source location, command,
    phase and time, without saving the raw configuration, nonce or exception content. Deduplicate by
    command and error code, at most 16 entries per run; a later CLEANED keeps the first failure. When
    ownership or log writing cannot be confirmed, report explicitly that it was not recorded; this must
    not replace the original refusal. The runner exposes only format-checked codes and source locations.
- Reboot scope:
  - before plan and injection confirm the HyperPod/EKS identity, Region, account, Node UID, provider
    instance, `NodeRecovery=None` and the actual Executor identity. After the reboot re-check the
    original instance and Deployment/template; a normal Executor Pod replacement is allowed, but another
    node or release is not accepted.
  - CloudTrail keeps the success/failure status, the full role ARN, cluster, node list, event and
    request IDs; the successful submission and the completed command must cover only the single
    approved node. A wrong cluster, multiple nodes, a failed call or ambiguous evidence cannot pass
    merely because "one reboot was found".
    The standard `dryRun=false` filled in by AWS may participate in the proof; `true`, non-boolean
    values or duplicate aliases cannot prove a real reboot.
  - the current runtime does not persist the AWS RequestId, so the submission record and CloudTrail
    are correlated by strict scope and the submission time window, without claiming an exact RequestId
    link. A negative CloudTrail conclusion within the visibility window remains marked provisional and
    is supplemented by a later full-window audit.
- ⚠ **This alternative path is not non-destructive.** The `gpu_inventory_mismatch` production policy
  plans `REBOOT_NODE`; as long as workflow execution is allowed, a real HyperPod reboot is invoked.
  This item must be executed as `destructive-provider-reboot` in the maintenance window, with a
  byte-level configuration backup, command cancellation and the formal restore procedure prepared in
  advance. The historical "safe alternative path" wording may no longer be used.




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-005

**The collection layer of the fabric-manager collector: cursor and the real log file**

- Formal entry: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_acceptance.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-005`.
- Purpose: verify production FM file collection, the persistent cursor and a process restart that
  keeps the cursor. The Store's upsert/idempotency can hide duplicate sends, so an unchanged number of
  stored rows alone cannot prove the absence of replay.
- Steps:
  1. Find the real path of the online fabric manager log and the collection method
     (journal unit or file + offset cursor).
  2. When the file source is enabled for the first time, confirm that the state directly records the
     current device, inode and EOF, and that historical SXIDs already in the file produce no events;
     then **append** to that source one unknown, Non-fatal SXID 99999 with a unique marker;
     this code is used only for collection and cursor verification and must not generate a node change
     workflow.
  3. Before injection save the real FM process's complete ROUND receipt as the journal cursor anchor.
     After the control plane receives the unique record, verify ATTEMPT, DELIVERED COMPLETION and the
     subsequent successful ROUND by its producer record ID digest; BUFFERED only means the outbox took
     over and is not proof of delivery.
  4. Confirm that the original cursor has reached the file EOF, then perform the approved collector
     restart. Bind the new systemd InvocationID/MainPID, read the complete journal window including the
     original anchor, and require the new process's first two actually completed rounds starting from
     sequence number 1 to have a cumulative source delivery of zero and no re-send of the original
     record digest.
  5. Keep sampling the receipt window, cursor and Store; the Store row count is used only for
     persistence verification and cannot replace producer evidence.
- Verdict: the event arrived, no workflow was generated, the cursor is persisted, and there is no
  source-layer replay within the bounded window above.
  Receipts are strictly bound to the cluster/node/boot/source-config digest, process and consecutive
  sequence numbers; a lost journal anchor, truncation, growth of budget omissions, counter exhaustion,
  failed rounds or unpaired sends must not PASS.
  Without production receipts, the restart must not proceed and a pass must not be issued on the
  strength of the old cursor or database row counts alone.
- By default no log is written for every empty 5-second round: it records the first two rounds after
  startup, budget-limited event receipts and cumulative progress at the health summary interval. The
  proof extends only to the last complete ROUND, promises no replay-free unbounded future, and does not
  treat one producer sink ACK as strict exactly-once downstream execution.
### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-022

**Post-deployment FM collector private-cursor loss, corruption and log-rotation recovery**

- Risk is `live-non-destructive`; the formal predecessor is COLLECT-005. Use the
  checked entry point `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collect022_fm_cursor_recovery.py`:
  plan first, then execute through explicit confirmation, node and maintenance window. Running the host probe directly is forbidden.
- Inside a UID-bound HostProbe, invoke the currently deployed `FabricManagerLogCollector`;
  the log, the cursor and the record sink all live in a private directory exclusive to this run. The sink does not forward to the CPU side, and the private directory
  must not point at the real fabric-manager log, collector state or service configuration.
- Verify in sequence: first-EOF baseline without a checkpoint; append A is delivered exactly once;
  a restart that keeps the checkpoint does not replay A; after deleting only the private checkpoint, the historical A is not replayed and a new B
  is still delivered; after corrupting the private checkpoint, old data is likewise not replayed; finally rotate and truncate the private log,
  the new marker continues and is delivered exactly once. The truncation must reuse the zero offset of the `active.log` that already emitted N,
  writing a shorter T on the same device/inode; the historical offset skipped by the initial EOF baseline may not be used in its place.
  Check the original N receipt, generation incremented by one, record ID/evidence_ref changed,
  and the other rotated log keeping its original bytes; record device, inode, offset, generation and counts separately for each phase.
- Verdict: must come from the real parser/cursor implementation of the deployed version; a preset result list may not stand in for it.
  Markers of this run must correspond exactly to the records; an unknown phase, empty output, duplicate or missing marker each fail.
- Verify that the actual Collector/Agent identity and real service state are unchanged. After stopping the private process,
  clean up only the private files, scripts, Pods and ConfigMaps owned by the nonce/UID; any `host_script`,
  `creation_unresolved` or other residue being true fails.
- COLLECT-005 checks the production collection chain and a restart with the cursor preserved; this case checks private-cursor fault recovery.
  The two share the parser but do not have the same injection boundary and cannot substitute for each other. A private software log is not a hardware
  SXID, nor does it serve as evidence that control-plane ingest, notification or physical recovery passed.
  A process restart within the same boot continues the original identity; a rename inherits the identity of the corresponding inode.
  A complete truncate/rewrite between two polls that cannot be observed is not part of the atomic log-write guarantee,
  and a lost checkpoint cannot recover history that was skipped.

### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-006

**NVLink5 decode table (XID 144-150): full coverage of all 95 rules**

- Purpose: fulfil the **full SXID decode-layer coverage** half of
  "every XID and SXID test must be covered".
  `spec.nvlink5.decodeRules` has **95 rules** in total;
  each maps `(xid, IntrInfo bit pattern, Error Status)`
  to a `recoveryAction`;
  if one rule decodes wrongly, the corresponding class of hardware fault is **silently misjudged**.
- Why **table-driven full coverage** is required instead of sampling:
  of the 95 rules, 40 are `IGNORE`, 40 are `RESET_GPU`,
  8 are `XID_154_EVAL`; sampling cannot detect **bit patterns shadowing each other**
  (a wider pattern swallowing a narrower one after it).
- Coverage elements (`src/gpu_fault/policy/ _workflow_nvlink5`):
  1. missing any one of `driver_branch` / `intr_info` / `error_status`
     → `BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE`, **no guessing**;
  2. `is_v1 = driver_branch < driverBoundary` (measured as **575**)
     decides between `v1Pattern` and `v2Pattern`
     → **every rule must run once on each branch**;
  3. `_pattern_matches` (`:2227`) compares the 32-bit mask bit by bit,
     `-` is a wildcard;
  4. `_error_status_matches` (`:2238`) supports
     **slash-separated multi-values** such as `0x00000000/0xFFFFFFFF`
     → multi-value rules must **run once per value**;
  5. action priority `RESET_GPU` > `XID_154_EVAL` > pure `IGNORE`;
     any other combination → `BLOCKED_WORKFLOW` requiring manual intervention;
  6. `action2` + `action2V*Pattern` are **additive actions**
     (present on the 3 `RLW_RXPIPE` rules); on a match they are merged into the action set.
- Verdict: all 95 rules × 2 driver branches × every declared Error Status value of each rule are exercised;
  each case asserts three things -- `official_action` equals the **independently recomputed** expected value,
  the rule's `subcode_name` appears in `matched_decode_rules`,
  `disposition` is not `BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE`;
  in addition a table-level invariant asserts that no rule is shadowed by another rule and that the rule count is exactly 95.
  The moment the expected value is changed to "ask the engine", this case is void -- the expected value would then be wrong together with the engine.




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-007

**XID catalog 172 rules × 4 product families: full coverage of the decision layer + all workflow branches**

- Purpose: fulfil the **XID half** of "every XID and SXID test must be covered".
  `COLLECT-006` already covers the NVLink5/SXID decode layer;
  this case covers **all decision branches** of `src/gpu_fault/policy/ _resolve_xid`.
- Why the matrix is built as "**rule × product family**" rather than only running the 78 H100 rules:
  `catalog_supports_product` (`src/gpu_fault/policy/`)
  decides applicability **on each rule's own products column**,
  not via a global switch. Running H100 alone cannot test the direction
  "**should have been NOT_APPLICABLE but was executed**" --
  which is the dangerous direction (executing on an A100 an action valid only for GB200).
  Hence **172 × 4 = 688** cases, each asserting the
  `(official_action, disposition, action)` triple.
- The expected values must be **independently recomputed**, using the same methodology as `COLLECT-006`:
  the test writes, following NVIDIA catalog semantics, its own
  `_expected_xid_outcome(rule, family)`,
  and **does not call** any helper from `src/gpu_fault/policy/`.
  Otherwise the expected value would be wrong together with the engine.
- Coverage elements (missing any one means a whole class of XIDs is silently misjudged):

  | # | Branch | Code location | How this case covers it |
  |---|------|---------|-------------|
  | 1 | XID not in catalog → `SITE_SAFETY` + `QUARANTINE` | `:786` | single case (xid 999) |
  | 2 | product family not applicable → `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `action=None` | `:802` | **347** cases in the matrix |
  | 3 | version gate missing evidence → `BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE` | `:1189` | 24 gated rules × missing driver / missing cuda |
  | 4 | version gate not satisfied → `NOT_APPLICABLE` | `:1239` | 24 rules × driver-1 / cuda-1 |
  | 5 | version gate exactly at the boundary → **must pass** | same as above | 24 rules (guards against "writing the boundary as `<=`") |
  | 6 | `immediateAction` empty → `MONITOR_ONLY` + `NO_ACTION` | `:836` | 30 cases in the matrix |
  | 7 | exact mapping of the four direct actions | `:853` `DIRECT_ACTION_MAP` | 278 matrix cases |
  | 8 | `WORKFLOW_XID_45` three branches | `:1380` | solo / with companion / window not closed |
  | 9 | `WORKFLOW_XID_48` three branches | `:1428` | solo / companion 63 / companion 64 |
  | 10 | `XID_154` six dynamic actions + window not closed | `:1332` | 7 cases |
  | 11 | `CHECK_UVM` three branches | `:1465` | uvm=None/True/False |
  | 12 | `WORKFLOW_NVLINK_ERR` (XID 74) evidence gate + non-Hopper refusal | `:918` | 2 cases |
  | 13 | unauthorised workflow → `BLOCKED_WORKFLOW` + `QUARANTINE` | `:904` | `RESTART_VM` (XID 151) + full-catalog scan asserting "the only action without an executor is exactly `RESTART_VM`" |
  | 14 | containment and pre_actions exceptions for XID 94/95 | `:2248` `:1276` | 2 cases |

  ⚠ **Why item 13 additionally needs a set-level assertion.**
  Non-direct actions are now dispatched through an `official action → resolver` table; any token
  not in the table is kept verbatim and becomes `BLOCKED_WORKFLOW`. That direction is safe, but **silent**:
  every event of that XID stops at manual handling. And the expected values of the 688 cases above are independently recomputed,
  with the recomputation logic likewise using "not in a known branch" as its fallback, so the engine and the expected value would **jointly**
  judge a new token as blocked, and the matrix would not notice. Therefore the whole catalog is additionally scanned, asserting that
  "the set of actions without an executor is exactly `{RESTART_VM}`" -- when a catalog upgrade introduces a new workflow
  it must be triaged, rather than discovering in production that some class of XID can from then on only be handled manually.

  ⚠ **Item 5 (boundary pass-through) is a deliberately added reverse assertion.**
  The version gate compares with `<`; writing it as `<=` would judge a real fault where
  "the driver just barely meets the minimum requirement" as `NOT_APPLICABLE` and silently discard it.
  Asserting only "lower versions are rejected" is **not enough** -- that assertion holds for `<=` too.
- Verdict: 172 rules × 4 product families, 688 cases in total; each case's
  `(official_action, disposition, action)` triple equals the **independently recomputed** expected value;
  the 14 branches in the table above are each covered; three mutations -- version gate `<` changed to `<=`,
  product-family membership check removed, `_xid_containment` simplified to always return `GPU` --
  must each turn the cases red, otherwise this batch of cases is not considered to bite.




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-008

**`WORKFLOW_XID_48` live double injection: XID 63 + XID 48 within the 30 s correlation window drive
`DRAIN_AND_RESET` through the real `/dev/kmsg`**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_destructive.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-008`.
- Level: `destructive` (performs a real GPU reset and quiesces kubelet).
- Goal: verify the multi-event correlation decision with real kmsg, rather than only verifying single-event API replay.
- Preconditions:
  - the kernel collector holds the `/dev/kmsg` fd, and the currently auto-discovered GPU product/driver/CUDA
    values satisfy the catalog version gates for XID 48/63;
  - `gpuReset` in the current Profile is an executable Node Agent owner; Agent readiness
    and the reset/quiesce/verify/restore capabilities are all Ready;
  - choose a clean idle node and read the real GPU BDF/UUID dynamically; record the ledger, timer,
    service, scheduling and GPU inventory baselines;
  - the host sampler must be detached from the Pod cgroup; the GPU sub-sampler carries a hard timeout and stops calling
    `nvidia-smi` once the quiesce timer is detected, so as not to become a reset client.
- Steps:
  1. Through the real `/dev/kmsg`, **inject XID 63 first, then within the 30-second correlation window inject
     XID 48 on the same GPU**; both messages use unique kernel event identifiers.
  2. Both pieces of evidence must carry `kmsg://<node>/<boot_id>/<sequence>`;
     product/driver/CUDA and the PCI→GPU resolution all come from the current node.
  3. Assert that XID 63 is `MONITOR_ONLY/IGNORE/NO_ACTION` and creates no workflow;
     XID 48 is `EXECUTABLE`, `official_action=DRAIN_AND_RESET`,
     `pre_actions=[MARK_UNSCHEDULABLE]`, `action=RESET_GPU`.
  4. Assert that all eight steps of the XID 48 reset workflow complete. The solo and companion
     branches have the same step sequence and must be distinguished by the decision field, not by the step count.
  5. The Node Agent ledger (exactly one RESET_GPU) and the host sampling (target GPU briefly unenumerable, then back to the expected count)
     together prove a single physical reset; the kernel journal excerpt serves as an additional record; the verdict contract is shared with DESTR-001,
     only the event is XID 48 and the official action is `DRAIN_AND_RESET`. Finally services, GPU inventory, scheduling state and
     timers return to baseline.
- Verdict: real collection layer, companion decision, single physical reset and automatic recovery all hold simultaneously.
- Rollback: if restore did not complete, recover the node through the formal validation/restore flow;
  do not delete the ownership annotations or the quarantine taint directly.

### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-009

**`CHECK_MECHANICALS` (XID 54) live run-through: `WAITING` → manual annotation confirmation
→ workflow completes directly**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_acceptance.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-009`.
- Level: `live-non-destructive`. The current design defines the mechanical check as a manual investigation:
  **no cordon, no taint, no GPU reset, no reboot, no job stop, no firmware flash**.
- Purpose: verify the complete closed loop `WAITING → manual confirmation → SUCCEEDED`, and the binding of the confirmation value to the
  incident/fencing token.
- Preconditions: choose a clean node with no historical non-terminal faults and no leftover isolation ownership; read the
  current BDF dynamically and confirm the kernel collector holds the `/dev/kmsg` fd.
- Steps:
  1. Record node Ready/scheduling/taints, boot ID, ledger, timers and GPU inventory.
  2. Inject XID 54 through the real `/dev/kmsg`; the evidence must carry `kmsg://`,
     and the decision is `EXECUTABLE/CHECK_MECHANICALS/action=None/requires_operator=true`.
  3. The workflow must be exactly
     `FREEZE_EVIDENCE → CHECK_MECHANICALS`; node state must not change while waiting.
  4. Wait at least three dispatcher cycles and confirm the step stays `WAITING`, with details containing the
     required annotation, the `<incident_id>:<fencing_token>` value,
     the acknowledgement command and the notification ID.
  5. First write a wrong fencing token; the step must remain `WAITING`; then run the correct command
     given in details; the step and the workflow must transition to `SUCCEEDED`.
  6. Ledger delta, temporary timers and provider mutations are all zero; boot ID and
     GPU inventory unchanged. Delete the test annotation.
- Verdict: the wrong confirmation is rejected, the correct confirmation completes, and there are no node side effects while waiting.
- The runner's marker can only hit the kmsg event and its decision; incident/workflow records carry no marker,
  so the workflow is correlated via "the incident points at the marked event" or "the marked decision names it";
  otherwise `WAITING` can never be observed. Also: `CHECK_MECHANICALS` is a step waiting for manual confirmation and
  must be excluded from the per-step cap of `GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_STEP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; otherwise
  it is judged FAILED after 10 minutes and escalated to ESCALATED (observed live).
- Under the regional architecture `CHECK_MECHANICALS` is a remote node action: the step `details` only hold
  `remote_command_id`/`remote_status` pointers; the required annotation, the
  `<incident_id>:<fencing_token>` value and the notification ID live in that remote command's
  `result_details`; the runner follows the pointers to read them (observed live).

### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-010

**The fail-closed branch of `UPDATE_SWFW` (XID 78): with no target firmware version configured it
must be blocked and must not quiesce the node**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_acceptance.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-010`.
- Level: `live-isolation` (only the reversible safety quarantine is executed; no quiesce,
  no firmware flash, no reset/reboot).
- Purpose: `UPDATE_SWFW` is **the only XID action class that actually flashes firmware**.
  Flashing firmware on a production GPU node is irreversible, and `§2.9` states explicitly "if any check fails,
  quarantine and the node is not returned to scheduling"; therefore this case only verifies the fail-closed direction,
  configures no firmware command and does not really flash.
- Preconditions: confirm on every control-plane replica that `GPU_FAULT_TARGET_FIRMWARE_VERSION` is not set;
  the target Node Agent must simultaneously have firmware allow=false and empty update/verify commands.
  No firmware gate may be opened temporarily in order to get this case through.
- Steps:
  1. After the node's preceding workflows reach terminal state, read the real BDF dynamically and inject
     XID 78 through `/dev/kmsg`.
  2. Assert the evidence carries `kmsg://` and the decision is
     `EXECUTABLE/UPDATE_SWFW/action=None/requires_operator=false`.
  3. The workflow ends `BLOCKED`, with reasons containing both the absence of an executable
     `softwareFirmwareUpdate` owner and the missing target firmware version; the official steps
     must not contain `UPDATE_SOFTWARE_FIRMWARE`.
  4. Wait at least three dispatcher cycles and confirm that only the reversible safety quarantine happened:
     no Node Agent ledger delta, kubelet/DCGM/Fabric Manager not stopped,
     no temporary timers, no reset/reboot, GPU inventory unchanged; evidence capture still complete.
- Verdict: fail-closed while the firmware gate is closed, and neither quiesce nor a firmware mutation was entered.
- Rollback: after the health snapshot and the formal `VALIDATE_GPU/HOST/FABRIC`, restore via
  `scripts/e2e/regional/restore_validated_quarantine.py`; do not
  uncordon or delete the ownership annotations directly.

### Shared preconditions for COLLECT-011 ~ 015 (**four real gaps**, written once, shared by the five cases)

These five cases fill the four real gaps that were explicitly listed earlier:

| Gap | Covering case | Previous status |
|---|---|---|
| SXID `SCOPE_DEPENDENT_RESET` (42 codes) | COLLECT-011 | unit tests only |
| SXID `ALWAYS_FATAL` → `REBOOT_NODE` (20 codes) | COLLECT-015 | unit tests only |
| SXID `RESET_ALL_GPUS_AND_NVSWITCHES` (10003/19084) | COLLECT-014 | fail-closed branch unit-tested only; positive path never run live |
| XID `RESTART_APP` (48 codes)/`RESET_GPU` (14 codes) via **real kmsg** | COLLECT-012 / 013 | API replay only; the front half of the collection layer (regex/dedup/permissions) never driven by these two classes |

#### Three key mechanisms derived from the dry run (written down before running, to avoid improvising on the spot)

1. **The ACCESS scope can only be obtained through the product invariant.**
   `NvidiaLogNormalizer._sxid_scope` **always returns `UNKNOWN`** (raw text is evidence, not trusted topology);
   `NvSwitchPortTopologyService.resolve` needs both `switch_id`
   **and** `port`, and `switch_id` is extracted only from
   `nvidia-nvswitch(\d+)\s*:`, `port` only from `\bLink\s+(\d+)\b`.
   Before running, read the current `nvswitch_port_topology`; only if there is no trusted topology at present
   can the scope come from the product invariant alone:
   port present + FATAL + product ∈ {H100,H200,H20}
   ⇒ `link_scope=ACCESS`, `link_scope_source=NVIDIA_PRODUCT_INVARIANT`.
   → **Whether the injected line carries the `nvidia-nvswitch<N>:` prefix directly decides which branch is taken**;
   these are precisely the two directions of COLLECT-011.
2. **`RESTART_APP` on an idle node can never proceed to execution past `EXECUTABLE`.**
   It is stopped by `workload restart/stop requires an affected workload or job ID`.
   To really drive execution of this class, the node must carry a real workload Pod
   (`DESTR-009` did this via the API path).
   → COLLECT-012 therefore **explicitly verifies only the front half of the collection layer + the SAFETY_PENDING decision**,
   without pursuing execution; this is a scope statement, not a failure.
3. **10003/19084 is a genuine whole-machine reset.**
   `fabricReset` in the current Profile must be `OWN`, the node side must have
   `GPU_FAULT_NODE_ALLOW_FABRIC_RESET=true`,
   `node_agent._reset_all_gpus_nvswitches` executes **`nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` without `-i`**
   (every GPU + NVSwitch on the machine),
   and the precondition requires `requested == local_inventory` to be exactly equal.
   → COLLECT-014 is done in two steps: first the fail-closed run (insufficient evidence), then the positive run.

### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-011

**SXID `SCOPE_DEPENDENT_RESET` (42 codes): real FM log injection,
both directions must fail-closed**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_acceptance.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-011`
  passing two different `--node` values.
- Level: `live-isolation` (both directions blocked; only the reversible safety quarantine is executed,
  no GPU reset/reboot).
- Gap covered: the 42 codes of `SCOPE_DEPENDENT_RESET`
  (11001,11009,11013,11018-11020,12001,12002,12022,12024-12027,
  12030-12032,14017,15001,15006,15009,15010,15012,15013,
  19047,19048,19054,19056,19058,19060,19061,19063,19064,19066,
  19067,19069,19070,20034,22012,24004-24007) previously had **unit tests only**.
- Purpose: pin down both entrances of the gate "**untrusted scope ⇒ do not dare touch the GPU**":
  (1) switch+port present ⇒ `ACCESS`, but an idle node cannot obtain
  `participating_gpu_uuids` ⇒ still blocked;
  (2) no switch ⇒ `UNKNOWN` ⇒ blocked directly with "missing trusted port-scope mapping".

#### Steps

1. Record the baseline: the FM log's current `size/inode/device` and the cursor JSON;
   the file cursor must equal the current end of file; if a rotation occurred, first record the new inode and offset;
   `unschedulable` / taints / annotations; the state of the six services; the `nvidia-smi -L` count.
2. Direction (1) (A1): append to `/var/log/fabricmanager.log`
   (append only; never delete or truncate the real log. Private truncation/generation verification happens only in COLLECT-022):
   ```
   [<ts>] [ERROR] [tid 990001] nvidia-nvswitch0: SXid \
   (PCI:0000:ab:00.0): 11001, Fatal, Link 12 NVLINK_FATAL_ERROR \
   marker=c011-a1-<ts>
   ```
   Note three hard requirements: the `nvidia-nvswitch0:` prefix (to obtain switch_id),
   `Link 12` (to obtain port), and `SXid (PCI:...): <code>, Fatal`
   with comma, space and parentheses exactly as written (to pass `SXID_SUMMARY_PATTERN`).
3. Assertion (1): evidence arrives (≤10 s, collection interval 5 s);
   decoded as `sxid=11001 cls=FATAL switch_id=0 port=12
   scope=ACCESS/NVIDIA_PRODUCT_INVARIANT nGPU=0`;
   decision `official=RESET_PARTICIPATING_GPUS`
   `disposition=BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE` `action=None`
   `safety=QUARANTINE` `cont=UNKNOWN` `operator=True`;
   workflow official 3 steps
   `FREEZE_EVIDENCE → COLLECT_DIAGNOSTIC_BUNDLE → QUARANTINE`.
   After the dispatcher has run the safety steps the terminal state must be `BLOCKED`;
   the intermediate `SAFETY_PENDING` of the dry run must not be taken as the final criterion.
4. Direction (2) (A2): using a **second clean GPU node**, append another line with the same code but
   **without the switch prefix**
   (`... NVSwitch SXid (PCI:0000:ab:00.0): 11001, Fatal, Link 12 ...`,
   with a different marker to avoid dedup).
   Waiting only for the terminal state of workflow (1) is not enough to isolate the two directions:
   a `QUARANTINED` incident may still become the correlation target of a new event on the same node while the marker is valid,
   so that A2 correctly produces an independent decision/marker but reuses the A1 incident
   and workflow. When A1/A2 must each be checked for the full workflow shape, different nodes are mandatory.
5. Assertion (2): `switch_id=None scope=UNKNOWN`,
   `nGPU=8` and `fabric_partition` synthesised
   (the inventory branch of `FaultIngestionService._enrich_sxid_scope`),
   `official=RESET_ALL_GPUS_AND_NVSWITCHES`
   `disposition=BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE`,
   reason **contains** `fatal SXID requires a trusted access/trunk
   port-scope mapping`; official 4 steps (one more than (1): `MARK_UNSCHEDULABLE`).
6. Then run both the ACCESS and UNKNOWN directions for 12001 and 24007 as well, three codes times two scopes in total.
   Each one re-verifies the idle-node and non-executable-reset scope premises, reads its own persisted
   decision/event ID, and confirms the exact sxid/classification/reason/workflow binding.
   Continue only after each variant has completed formal recovery; stop immediately when the previous one fails; a PASS on 11001
   may not stand in for the other two codes. The component matrix for the remaining catalog rules is kept separately and does not claim per-code live full coverage.
7. **Zero-destruction assertion**: all six services `active` throughout, `nvidia-smi -L` = 8,
   ledger delta 0; no temporary recovery/rollback timers other than the routine read-only
   `gpu-fault-certificate-check.timer`,
   and the timer set is unchanged before and after; `boot_id` unchanged.
  8. Save the cursor and log snapshots from before and after this append. No-replay on production restart is proven independently by COLLECT-005's
     send receipts; private state loss/corruption and truncation are proven by COLLECT-022.
     This case does not damage the real state again, and does not use "evidence count did not grow" in place of a sending-layer conclusion.
  9. The `PCI:` used by the runner for injection is a test switch BDF that cannot map to a real GPU
     (default `0000:ab:00.0`; pick another address if it collides with any GPU slot),
     and the read-only premises for scope/participating GPUs are verified before sending. It is not actual NVSwitch fault evidence, and
     a GPU's own BDF must never be used:
     `_enrich_sxid_scope` resolves the ACCESS scope to that GPU by PCI slot,
     `RESET_PARTICIPATING_GPUS` immediately becomes executable and really resets that GPU (observed live).
     FM events are not in the XID event table; the runner recovers the deterministic
     event ID from the raw FM evidence bound to the marker, then follows the persisted decision/event link, and does not guess ownership from the node's "latest workflow".
- Verdict: both directions of the three specified codes are blocked, exactly bound and without extra actions; collection and cursor proofs are recorded within the
  explicit independent scopes above, and component PASS does not substitute for the on-site variants.
- Rollback: `QUARANTINE` sets the node `unschedulable=true` and applies the
  `gpu-fault.io/quarantined` taint plus the three ownership annotations. After the run, restore with
  `scripts/e2e/regional/restore_validated_quarantine.py` once validation passes;
  do not delete the taint/annotations directly. The injected log lines remain in the file.




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-012

**XID `RESTART_APP` (48 codes, the largest class): switch from API replay to real kmsg injection**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_acceptance.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-012`.
- Level: `live-kernel-log-injection` (only writes XID lines to the real `/dev/kmsg`; an idle node
  is judged MONITOR_ONLY; no quarantine, no quiesce, no reboot, no job stop).
- Gap covered: these 48 `RESTART_APP` codes
  (8,11,13,25,31,32,39,40,41,60,68-72,75-77,80,82-86,88,89,94,
  96-105,126-135,139) previously **only went through API replay**;
  the kmsg collector's regex / dedup / permissions had never been driven by this class.
  The evidence record's id in the Store carries the collection-channel prefix (`nvidia-kernel/kmsg-<boot_id>-<sequence>`),
  and the `evidence_ref` produced by the collector (`kmsg://<node>/<boot_id>/<sequence>`) sits in the record's `payload`;
  the runner checks "two writes → two records, each with its own reference" against this storage shape.
- **Scope statement**: `RESTART_APP` names an application. An idle node has no managed application that can be stopped/restarted;
  since 55272a0 the policy judges `RESTART_APP` on IDLE as `MONITOR_ONLY`/`NO_ACTION`
  (INFO marker + investigation notification, **no workflow opened, no cordon**), and the incident converges directly to
  RECOVERED. This case verifies **the front half of the collection layer + the correctness of the idle-node decision**; it does not verify execution,
  and there is no longer a BLOCKED safety chain.

#### Steps

1. Baseline as in COLLECT-011 step 1 (additionally record the kernel collector MainPID
   and `/proc/<pid>/fd/3 -> /dev/kmsg`).
2. Real kmsg injection D1 (XID 13, unique pid):
   `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:59:00): 13, pid=931013, name=python,
   Graphics Exception: ... marker=c012-d1-<ts>`
   written to `/dev/kmsg` (`<3>` priority prefix, same technique as
   `scripts/e2e/regional/manifests/fault-injection/kmsg-xid63-xid48.yaml`).
3. Assert the collection layer: the line is visible in `dmesg`; the evidence `record_id`
   has the form `kmsg-<boot_id>-<sequence>`, `evidence_ref =
   kmsg://<node>/<boot_id>/<sequence>`, where the boot ID must equal the current baseline recorded in
   step 1; product/driver/CUDA in `fields` must equal the target node's
   current auto-discovered values.
4. Assert identity semantics: **write exactly the same text to `/dev/kmsg` again**.
   The kernel assigns a new sequence, so a second, different `record_id` must be formed;
   identical text is not the same kernel event. True duplicate dedup uses the isolated replay fixture to replay
   the same raw sequence and must produce evidence only once.
5. Assert the decision: `official=RESTART_APP` `disposition=MONITOR_ONLY`
   `action=NO_ACTION`, `reasons` **contains** `no managed application to restart`
   (the idle node has no application to restart).
6. Assert the absence of a safety chain: **no workflow at all** (no more `blocked_reasons`,
   no more BLOCKED terminal state); the incident converges to `RECOVERED` and
   `workflow_request_id` is empty; the node stays Ready, schedulable and free of `gpu-fault.io` taints throughout.
   Use "decision recorded + incident RECOVERED" as the terminal signal when waiting for convergence;
   do not wait for a workflow (none is produced at all).
7. Inject D2 (XID 31, MMU fault, the most common code) and re-check the same conclusion. Since neither injection
   quarantines the node, **no** validated restore is needed in between; the two XIDs are injected back to back.
8. **Zero-destruction assertion** as in COLLECT-011 step 7 (six services active, boot_id unchanged).
- Verdict: the kmsg collection chain works end to end (record_id/evidence_ref/triple all present)
  + dedup behaviour recorded + idle-node decision MONITOR_ONLY/NO_ACTION with no workflow
  + zero node changes.
- Rollback: none -- this case does not quarantine the node; there is no isolation to lift.




### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-013

**XID `RESET_GPU` (14 codes): real kmsg injection that **really** executes a single-GPU reset**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_destructive.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-013`.
  `--xid {109,62}` (default `109`) selects the RESET_GPU-class XID injected in this round; one round injects once and
  performs exactly one real single-GPU reset.
- Level: `destructive` (**quiesces the node, including stopping kubelet**).
- Gap covered: these 14 `RESET_GPU` codes
  (46,62,64,95,109,110,119,120,136,140,143,155,156,158)
  previously had API replay only. Live, it is only necessary to prove that **one** RESET_GPU-class XID can drive a
  real single-GPU reset from real kmsg; the decision semantics of the remaining codes are covered by the `GF-LIVE-KMSG-*` family and the
  XID catalog rule replay of `COLLECT-007`; no second reset is performed per code.
- ⚠⚠ **`QUIESCE_GPU_SERVICES` stops kubelet**
  (`GPU_FAULT_QUIESCE_SERVICES` includes kubelet),
  so `kubectl exec` disconnects midway. **Before injecting**, start a host-side sampler with
  `nohup setsid` that writes the whole process to a file under
  `/var/log/` (same technique as DESTR-001 / COLLECT-008),
  otherwise no evidence from the quiesce period can be obtained.
- The sampler's short-lived `nvidia-smi -L` may collide with
  `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset`. It is correct for `VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS` to let through clients that do not persist across
  samples, but the reset must additionally handle the TOCTOU window after the check.
  The current Node Agent performs at most 3 bounded retries only for the driver's explicit
  `In use by another client`, re-running the fail-closed client check before each retry;
  other reset errors still fail immediately, and a persistent occupant fails once the limit is reached.
  **Do not sidestep this race by stopping the sampler**, or the core evidence of this case is lost.

#### Steps

1. Baseline as above; additionally confirm `ALLOW_GPU_RESET=true`,
   `ALLOW_SERVICE_QUIESCE=true`, and `gpuReset` in the profile is `OWN`.
2. **Start the host sampler first** (detached, one round per second, recording the state of the six services,
   the `nvidia-smi -L` count, `unschedulable`, ledger, boot_id).
3. Real kmsg injection E1 (default XID 109, `Context Switch Timeout Error`; `--xid 62` switches to the other
   RESET_GPU-class code).
4. Assert the decision: `official=RESET_GPU` `disposition=EXECUTABLE`
   `action=RESET_GPU`, workflow **`PENDING` with
   `blocked_reasons=[]`**, the required reset dependency chain as in the shared preconditions table;
   incident `state=ACTION_PENDING`.
   ⚠ If `BLOCKED_MISSING_EVIDENCE` + "Catalog compatibility gate
   requires driver_branch, cuda_version" appears, the collector's triple was lost;
   **that is an environment problem, not a policy defect**; fix the triple first and rerun.
5. Assert execution: the ledger shows `QUIESCE_GPU_SERVICES` →
   `VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS` → `RESET_GPU` (**with `-i <index>`, single GPU**)
   → `RESTORE_GPU_SERVICES` → `VALIDATE_GPU` → `RESTORE_SCHEDULING`,
   all `SUCCEEDED`.
6. Assert recovery: the sampler file shows kubelet going `active` → stopped → back to `active`;
   finally all six services `active`, `nvidia-smi -L` back to 8 GPUs,
   `unschedulable` lifted by `RESTORE_SCHEDULING`, `boot_id` **unchanged**
   (a single-GPU reset does not reboot the machine).
7. No second XID is injected: the remaining RESET_GPU codes are covered by the `GF-LIVE-KMSG-*` family and
   the XID catalog replay of `COLLECT-007`; this case performs this one reset only.
- Verdict: one real-kmsg RESET_GPU-class XID drives **exactly one** real single-GPU reset with automatic return to scheduling;
  `boot_id` unchanged; evidence from the quiesce period is fully preserved by the host-side sampler.
- Rollback: normally `RESTORE_SCHEDULING` completes automatically;
  on a mid-way failure, first confirm the physical result and the product's compensation, and keep the isolation/manual reconciliation when unknown.
  Do not complete the runner cleanup by directly restoring the six services, clearing the quiesce state or uncordoning.


### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-014

**SXID `RESET_ALL_GPUS_AND_NVSWITCHES` (10003/19084):
the action class that runs `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` over every GPU and NVSwitch of the machine**

- Formal entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collector_destructive.py --case GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-014`.
- Level: `destructive` (whole-machine reset of every GPU + NVSwitch; quiesces the node).
- Gap covered: this class requires **dual evidence: `fabric_partition` + complete GPU inventory**;
  the fail-closed branch previously had **unit tests only**, and the positive path had never been run live.
- Fail-closed first, then the two positive variants 10003/Fatal and 19084/Non-fatal in turn.
  The plan explicitly lists two reset cycles; each variant has its own marker, decision, ledger and sampling evidence.
  By default, reusing the same node requires formal recovery, a 60-second cooldown and three complete stable inventory/clean-node
  reads; if the previous variant did not pass or its result is unknown, do not continue.

#### Steps

1. Baseline as above; confirm `fabricReset` is `OWN`,
   `ALLOW_FABRIC_RESET=true`, and the agent's `allowed_operations` includes
   `RESET_ALL_GPUS_NVSWITCHES`; record the full set of GPU UUIDs matching the site-declared count
   (`node_agent._reset_all_gpus_nvswitches` requires
   `requested == local_inventory` to be exactly equal; one missing means refusal).
2. **Fail-closed direction**: construct a 10003 but leave the inventory evidence incomplete.
   The current `_enrich_sxid_scope` prefers the independent mandatory
   `gpu_inventory_snapshot` (delivered every 60 s by default, 180 s freshness) and falls back to the legacy metrics inventory (600 s by default) only when the snapshot is missing.
   Both sources require
   `event.observed_at - inventory.observed_at >= -30s`;
   use a currently ACTIVE node whose lease has not expired and set the event time to `now - 8min`;
   do not mix in identity errors by using a retired/REVOKED node. Before sending, read both the dedicated and legacy inventories;
   every existing sample must be at least 90 seconds newer than the event (30 s ingestion tolerance plus a 60 s safety margin);
   unknown presence/time or an unmet margin means do not send. Merely backdating the time does not by itself prove the premise.
   The event still stays within the 900-second generation cap, so it is not blocked by another stale-generation reason.
   The runner now also asserts a ledger delta of 0 and an unchanged `boot_id` during the fail-closed phase;
   if either is violated it FAILs immediately and injects no positive variant at all.
   Assert that `blocked_reasons` **contains exactly and only**
   `"SXID 10003 requires fabric_partition and complete node GPU inventory"`
   as the execution-gate-related reason,
   and that **no node-side action** occurred (ledger delta 0, all services active,
   `nvidia-smi -L`=8, `boot_id` unchanged).
   ⚠ API injection must use `dp_call` (token read from the executor Pod environment);
   the endpoint `POST /v1/collector-events/fabric-manager` requires both the
   `X-GPU-Fault-Cluster-ID` **and** the regional bearer header;
   missing either yields 401.
3. **Positive direction**: append C1 to the target node's FM log:
   ```
   [<ts>] [ERROR] [tid 990003] nvidia-nvswitch0: SXid \
   (PCI:0000:ab:00.0): 10003, Fatal, Link 3 \
   NVSWITCH_NON_CORRECTABLE marker=c014-c1-<ts>
   ```
   Start the detached host sampler **before** injecting (as in COLLECT-013).
4. Assert the decision: `official=RESET_ALL_GPUS_AND_NVSWITCHES`
   `disposition=EXECUTABLE` `action=None` `cont=FABRIC_PARTITION`
   `operator=False`; `nGPU` equals the site-declared expected GPU count;
   workflow `PENDING`, `blocked_reasons=[]`, the required dependency chain as in the shared preconditions table;
   the `RESET_ALL_GPUS_NVSWITCHES` step has
   `execution_owner=gpu-fault-node-agent`,
   `parameters={'fabric_partition':
   '<cluster>/<node>/local-nvswitch', 'sxid': 10003}`,
   and `gpu_uuids` exactly equal to the machine's complete inventory.
5. Assert execution: `RESET_ALL_GPUS_NVSWITCHES` `SUCCEEDED` in the ledger;
   node-side evidence shows that **`nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` without `-i`** was executed;
   the post-reset inventory re-check still yields the same full UUID set
   (node_agent verifies this once more itself).
6. Assert recovery: `RESTORE_GPU_SERVICES` → `VALIDATE_GPU` →
   `VALIDATE_FABRIC` → `RESTORE_SCHEDULING` all `SUCCEEDED`;
   six services back to active, GPU count back to the site-declared value, `boot_id` **unchanged**,
   fabricmanager restarted with no new FATAL SXID.
7. Add C2 (19084, Non-fatal but the same whole-machine reset class) --
   **this one proves "non-fatal may also trigger a whole-machine reset"**,
   i.e. the action class is decided by the rule, not the severity. The current runner, after C1 passes and formal recovery completes,
   cools down on the same node as planned and obtains three stable readings; any change in the full UUID set, boot, Ready, ownership or workload
   is refused. C2's step parameters must keep `sxid=19084`; C1's success record may not be reused.
- Verdict: no action in the negative direction; each of the two specified positive variants succeeds once and completes product recovery. Component classification tests and real
  resets are recorded separately; a 10003 success does not automatically prove 19084.
- Rollback: normally automatic recovery; on failure or an unknown result keep the protections per this group's shared cleanup constraints,
  and do not obtain a PASS by directly restoring services or uncordoning.
- ⚠ If `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset` fails while residual clients exist,
  the expectation is that `VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS` blocks first (fail-closed)
  rather than a hard reset failure -- record either outcome truthfully.


### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-016

**`RESTART_APP` / `RESET_GPU` under a real distributed training workload:
actually running to completion the execution segment that COLLECT-012 declares "unverified"**

- Independent formal entry point:
  `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collect016_training_recovery.py`.
- Level: `destructive` (deletes and recreates training Pods;
  segment D additionally quiesces the node, including stopping kubelet).
- ⚠⚠ **Must be ordered before COLLECT-015**: 015 really reboots the node,
  which would destroy the training job and the sampler together.

#### The real increment of this case (stated up front, to avoid duplicating existing cases)

The manual already has three adjacent pieces of coverage, but **none of them covers what this case must prove**:

| Existing | What it covers | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `COLLECT-012` | the **decision** for `RESTART_APP` driven by real kmsg | an idle node is MONITOR_ONLY/NO_ACTION and produces no workflow; real application stop and recovery not verified |
| `DESTR-009` | real execution of `STOP_WORKLOADS`/`RESTART_WORKLOAD` | injection goes through **API replay** (`/v1/collector-events/nvidia-kernel`), skipping the front half of the collection layer |
| `COLLECT-013` | real execution of `RESET_GPU` driven by real kmsg | does not cover the full chain of an active workload being STOPped first, then a physical reset, then restarting the same job |

⇒ The three things this case must prove all lie in the intersection gap of the three above:

1. **The positive branch of `_enrich_fault_identity`** (`src/gpu_fault/app/`):
   the kmsg event itself carries **no** job/attempt; via
   `ctx.topology.resolve()` the `job_id`/`attempt_id`/`affected_workload_ids`
   are looked up back from the attempt observation, and
   `workload_identity_source` must be **`SOLE_ACTIVE_ATTEMPT_ON_NODE`**
   (not `NO_ACTIVE_MANAGED_ATTEMPT` -- which is exactly the value COLLECT-012 obtains).
   This code path previously had **no live positive evidence at all**.
2. **Real reservation of `restart_budget` / attempt ownership**:
   `reserve_restart_budgets` in `restart_budget_preflight.py` really calls
   `reserve_job_restart` once at claim time,
   `restart_count` goes 0→1; a second injection must report
   **`RESTART_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`** (`--restart-budget 1`).
3. **The physical action order for an active workload really closes**:
   when segment D injects XID 109 (`RESET_GPU`), torchrun processes are running on all 8 GPUs.
   The current workflow always executes `STOP_WORKLOADS` first, then
   `QUIESCE_GPU_SERVICES → VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS → RESET_GPU`;
   therefore one cannot claim that VERIFY first sees the training client and quiesce then lets it through.
   The positive increment of this segment is to prove that the workload stops first, the no-client gate passes after quiesce,
   the reset executes and the workload restarts. The fail-closed behaviour for a persistent client is verified by an independent LOCAL contract;
   the current live segment D does not deploy that negative holder.

#### LOCAL negative evidence

The preflight's `LOCAL_CONTRACT_SELECTORS` cover four groups -- reset/restart, DCGM classification, control-plane action selection
and client intersection -- 14 selectors in total. A complete pytest receipt, bounded to 300 seconds and bound to the source,
records setup/call/teardown; a missing item, skip, filtering or an incomplete receipt cannot satisfy the local gate.
This includes CONFIG, CONFIG mixed with isolation-level errors, missing severity, parse error/INCONCLUSIVE,
current and compatible Agent results, active-workload execution review, plus short-lived respawn and persistent clients.

The output `local-contracts.json` states explicitly `validation_level=LOCAL`,
`live_negative_actions_performed=false`, kept separate from segment D's `live-positive-XID109-reset`.
The on-site negative behaviour of these mechanisms is not measured by this runner; local coverage must not be rewritten as LIVE, nor may
GPU hardware damage be inflicted or a forbidden persistent holder be deployed to pad the numbers.

#### Preconditions

1. **Image prewarming is a structural necessity, not a stopgap** (DESTR-009 supplement 6):
   the init container auto-injected by training-operator waits only **200 seconds**
   (`100 × sleep 2`), while a single 7.99 GB layer ÷ 39 MB/s ≈ 205 seconds
   is already the theoretical lower bound ⇒ any first pull is bound to fail.
   First start the `gf-training-image-prepull` DaemonSet on all current candidate nodes
   (**not requesting
   `nvidia.com/gpu`**, otherwise it competes with the 24-GPU job for resources);
   the criterion is that `.status.images` of every candidate node shows `cached=True`,
   not the Pod status.
2. **Must be submitted with `gpu-training-submit`, not by `kubectl apply` of the fixture**:
   the fixture itself does not report attempt observations; the observation of the 24 GPU UUIDs
   is produced by the completion-watcher from the labels/annotations injected by the CLI.
   Without it, the whole chain of increment 1 cannot be established.
3. **An old job of the same name must be deleted first**: for an existing object the CLI outputs
   `configured` (not `created`), only updates labels and **does not recreate Pods**.
4. **The job name must not reuse DESTR-009's `gpu-fault-xid11-three-node`**
   (to avoid confusion with dedup/ownership of historical incidents); this case uses
   `gpu-fault-c016-three-node`.
5. **Observation freshness**: `WorkloadTopologyService.max_age_seconds
   = 120` (`telemetry.py:150`), while the completion-watcher's
   `watch_timeout=30s` re-lists and reconciles at the start of each round
   ⇒ a steadily running job refreshes its observation every ≤30 s,
   landing stably inside the 120 s window. **`workload_state=ACTIVE` must be confirmed before injecting**;
   it may not be assumed.
6. Dynamically select a target node that hosts the training task and has no non-terminal incident; record its
   BDF/UUID and boot ID; neither `RESTART_APP` nor `RESET_GPU` may change the boot ID.

#### Steps

1. Baseline: images cached on all candidate nodes; six services active; GPU count equals the site-declared value;
   `unschedulable`/taints/annotations empty; `boot_id`;
   kernel collector MainPID and `/proc/<pid>/fd/3 -> /dev/kmsg`.
2. Once the prewarm DaemonSet is ready, submit the 3-node 24-GPU PyTorchJob:
   ```bash
     gpu-training-submit --site "${SITE_FILE}" \
       scripts/e2e/regional/manifests/training/xid11-three-node-pytorchjob.yaml \
     --job-id "c016-${SUF}" \
     --attempt-id "attempt-c016-${SUF}-1" \
     --attempt-number 1 --restart-budget 1 \
     --namespace gpu-fault-system --context "${GPU_EKS_CONTEXT}"
   ```
   The fixture uses a workload name dedicated to this case with a unique suffix; old objects may not be reused.
   **The real "it is up" criterion**: all 3 Pods `1/1 Running`
   **and** the master log shows a `HEARTBEAT` containing `all_reduce=`.
   `ContainerCreating` for more than about 3 minutes is already a certain failure;
   stop waiting immediately and investigate the prewarm rather than keep observing.
3. Confirm the observation has reached the control plane and is parsed correctly:
   `workload_state=ACTIVE`, `job_id`/`attempt_id` match the submitted values,
   24 unique GPU UUIDs, `runtime_profile_version=${RUNTIME_PROFILE_VERSION}`,
   `restart_budget=1`; and the **target node** appears in
   `containers[].node_id` with `terminated=false`.
4. **Segment A (`RESTART_APP`, real kmsg)**: write XID 31 to the target node's
   `/dev/kmsg` (`RESTART_APP` class, same class as COLLECT-012's
   13/31 but with an independent marker):
   ```
   <3>NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:59:00): 31, pid=<uniq>, name=python, \
   Ch 00000008, intr 10000000. MMU Fault ... marker=c016-a1-<ts>
   ```
5. **Segment A assertions (the core of this case)**:
   - collection layer: `record_id=kmsg-<boot_id>-<seq>`,
     `evidence_ref=kmsg://...`, product/driver/CUDA equal to the current baseline of step 1;
   - **identity completion**: the event's
     `workload_identity_source=SOLE_ACTIVE_ATTEMPT_ON_NODE`,
     `job_id=c016-<SUF>`, `attempt_id=attempt-c016-<SUF>-1`,
     `affected_workload_ids` non-empty, `workload_state=ACTIVE`;
   - **gate pass-through**: `official_action=RESTART_APP`,
     `disposition=EXECUTABLE`, **`blocked_reasons=[]`**
     (contrast COLLECT-012's idle MONITOR_ONLY; this segment additionally has a fresh, unambiguous managed attempt
     and full stop/recovery authorisation; a single status string is not enough);
   - steps: `FREEZE_EVIDENCE → STOP_WORKLOADS →
     RESTART_WORKLOAD` all `SUCCEEDED`,
     with the step parameters of `RESTART_WORKLOAD`
     `job_id` = the real job (**not `unknown`**),
     `source_gpu_count=24` (**not 0**), `restart_budget=1`;
   - delegation: if the step is still `WAITING` at sampling time, `details` contains
     `"mutation_submitted_by_control_plane": false`; if already terminal,
     `adapter_operation_id=remote/<command-id>` with the corresponding remote command
     in state `SUCCEEDED` is equivalent evidence. The executor log shows the corresponding `command_id`,
     and **the control-plane Pod logs contain no workload write operation within the time window after injection**
     (evidence capture must use a time-window delta, otherwise historical lines are hit);
   - execution effect: all 3 old Pod UIDs disappear, 3 new Pods come up,
     all_reduce of the new attempt resumes, target GPU count still 24;
   - **budget**: `restart_count` of
     `GET /v1/restart-budgets/<cluster>/<job>` goes 0→1.
6. **Segment B (budget exhausted)**: after segment A has recovered, inject another XID of the same class
   (new marker/pid). The current implementation runs the budget preflight before the adapter executes and revokes the restart step whose budget is exhausted:
   before injecting, wait until only the restart attempt remains as the single `RUNNING` record inside topology's 120-second observation window;
   A's old RUNNING snapshot is still legitimately visible during a brief overlap, and injecting immediately at that point
   correctly yields `AMBIGUOUS_ACTIVE_ATTEMPTS`;
   the budget gate would still take effect, but that cannot be used for this segment's single-attempt identity assertion.
   Assert that the workflow ends `FAILED` and records
   `RESTART_WORKLOAD / RESTART_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, without dispatching or completing `RESTART_WORKLOAD`.
   Evidence capture and the `STOP_WORKLOADS` remediation may still execute and produce corresponding remote commands; one may not require all commands to be 0,
   nor make "training Pods completely unchanged" a condition of budget protection; `restart_count` must stop at 1,
   and no new recovery attempt may be created. Missing or malformed command or execution-result reports do not constitute evidence of "no restart".
7. **Segment C (zero over-reach)**: throughout A/B
   `nvidia-smi -L`=8, `boot_id` unchanged, no quarantine taint,
   no `BatchReplaceClusterNodes` in CloudTrail,
   no GPU reset / reboot. ⚠ Interpretation point as in COLLECT-012 supplement 3:
   "did not happen" here means **the policy itself does not plan** these actions,
   not that a guard intercepted them -- the two kinds of "did not happen" must be distinguished.
8. **Segment D (positive XID109 reset closed loop on an active workload)**:
   after segment B, first delete the A/B fixture workload and wait for the recorded source attempt and recovery attempt to leave the node's ownership.
   The wait cap is 600 seconds, further bounded by this maintenance window and the parent deadline; use the actually returned job/attempt identities
   and do not re-assemble names. Empty, malformed, cross-cluster/cross-job Observation reports or ones lacking the known attempt may not pass;
   a non-terminal record with only some ranks terminated may not be regarded as drained either. If draining fails, segment D injection must not start.
   Then the job must be re-submitted with a **new Kubernetes workload name and a new job ID**
   and all_reduce allowed to stabilise. The restart budget is accounted per job ID;
   reusing A/B's job ID would be blocked by step 6's budget preflight before any quiesce/reset,
   and the physical chain of segment D could not be tested at all.
   **Start the detached host sampler first** (one round per second, flush every round;
   quiesce stops kubelet and disconnects `kubectl exec`),
   then inject XID 109 (`RESET_GPU` class) into `/dev/kmsg`.
   Assertions:
   - the step order must be `STOP_WORKLOADS → QUIESCE_GPU_SERVICES →
     VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS → RESET_GPU`; the evidence for STOP is that all old Pod UIDs disappear,
     and after a successful quiesce VERIFY should go straight to `SUCCEEDED`. If a transport-layer
     `WAITING` is misreported as "saw the training client", that evidence is invalid;
   - `RESET_GPU` **with `-i <index>` (single GPU)**,
     not the whole-machine `--gpu-reset` (contrast COLLECT-014);
   - in the sampler, kubelet `active → stopped → back to active`;
   - final state: six services active, `nvidia-smi -L`=8, `boot_id` unchanged,
     `unschedulable`/taints/annotations cleared.
   - **It is forbidden to run the negative test live with a holder that keeps `/dev/nvidia*` open long-term.**
     That injection may cause the driver to keep removing the device after the holder exits, exceeding the reversible acceptance boundary;
     the TOCTOU negative may only be covered in Node Agent unit tests/the simulated runner.
   - `RUN_DCGM_DIAGNOSTIC` and quiesce/reset both depend on the GPU runtime.
     The registry already makes them share the `GPU_RUNTIME_MUTATION` claim; a concurrent host finding
     may only queue as a successor; merging the dcgmi branch into a reset DAG that is stopping DCGM is forbidden.
     Purely read-only `FREEZE_EVIDENCE` / `VALIDATE_*` branches may be merged into the DAG,
     or completed independently as predecessor successors; as long as there is no second
     `QUIESCE/RESET/RUN_DCGM_DIAGNOSTIC` physical branch, it does not count as a resource conflict.
9. Cleanup: delete the training job to release the 24 GPUs, delete the `gf-training-image-prepull`
   DaemonSet (the image layers stay on the nodes; the prewarm effect persists),
   stop the sampler and run `systemctl reset-failed` to clear one-shot unit residue,
   and check that the node is back to Ready and schedulable.
- Verdict: each of the three increments holds --
  (1) `SOLE_ACTIVE_ATTEMPT_ON_NODE` + `blocked_reasons=[]` +
  real job_id/24 GPUs (contrast COLLECT-012's idle monitor-only);
  (2) `restart_count` 0→1 and `RESTART_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` on the second injection;
  (3) the active workload is STOPped first, then quiesce/no-client/reset, and recovered by a new attempt;
  the second no-client gate inside reset is covered by unit tests, without using a dangerous holder to build a live negative.
- Rollback: delete the job + clean up the sampler; if the node does not self-heal after quiesce,
  first check the complete state per the shared recovery guard, and keep the operator hold when the result is unknown.
  GPU services may not be restored directly, in-flight action occupancy released or isolation lifted for the sake of cleanup.


#### Runner behaviour notes (corrected after the first live run)

- Segment A reuses `run_destr009_workload_restart.workflow_errors`; that contract originally hard-coded
  XID 11 (DESTR-009's replay code); this case injects a real kmsg XID 31, now passed in via
  `xid=31`, with the remaining RESTART_APP assertions unchanged.
- Segment D reuses the required dependency-chain check of `run_destr001_gpu_reset.workflow_errors`:
  `STOP_WORKLOADS` must precede quiesce, and `RESTART_WORKLOAD` must follow the return to scheduling.
  Registered, scope-limited read-only branches are allowed; the whole workflow's length and operation list no longer have to be identical;
  extra physical actions, missing barriers or unfinished dependencies still fail.
- WAITING evidence: if a step completes within one store poll (about 11 s), WAITING cannot be observed,
  and the terminal record no longer carries `mutation_submitted_by_control_plane`; the contract now accepts a terminal
  `adapter_operation_id` starting with `remote/` as equivalent evidence (the same fact: the mutation was executed by the GPU-side
  executor, not by the control plane). QUIESCE_GPU_SERVICES on the first run was exactly this.

### GF-REGIONAL-COLLECT-017

**Live verification of layered EFA recovery and Kubernetes accelerator allocatable**

- Independent official entry point: `scripts/e2e/regional/run_collect017_efa_plugin.py`.
- Level: `live-node-mutation`. No node reboot/replace is performed, but one EFA
  PCI function is really unbound, and EFA/NVIDIA device-plugin Pods are really deleted.
- The target version is defined by `gpu-fault-release-metadata.required-agent-artifact-sha256`
  and the current content-addressed wheel; historical fixed hashes must not be reused.
- The NVIDIA/EFA plugin DaemonSets chosen for segments B/C must be configured as
  `OnDelete` beforehand, per the approved maintenance deployment policy.
  `RollingUpdate` or an unknown strategy would spread the temporary affinity change to
  other nodes; the runner must refuse, and must not switch the update strategy to
  OnDelete online just to pass the precheck.
- Before temporarily excluding the target node, first create a GPU-local, least-privilege
  watchdog Job/ServiceAccount/Role/RoleBinding and confirm it is ARMED; it restores the
  original affinity at the 600-second boundary. The missing-value, null and
  multiple-required-affinity shapes of the original are each preserved; updates are bound
  to the UID and resourceVersion. If restore fails, the watchdog must not be cancelled and
  "cleaned up" must not be written; a same-name resource with a new UID, strategy drift,
  or another writer changing the affinity all stop further injection.

**Verdict**: for each of segments A/B/C, the "must observe / must generate / final" code
blocks match line by line; each segment's incident must converge to `RECOVERED`
(segment A additionally requires `workflow=SUCCEEDED`). The two paths listed under
